brandSystem:
MEAL DIRECT  /  CREATIVE PRODUCTION SYSTEM
Campus Campaign Design Prompt Library
28 detailed prompts for university specific social, recruitment, event, vendor and print designs
Built for flexible university names, verified local facts and custom QR destinations.
Use each prompt as a complete art direction brief. Replace every {{VARIABLE}} with approved campaign information before publication, composite the official Meal Direct logo and the real QR asset as placed layers, and remove any optional block whose supporting fact is unavailable.
BRAND SOURCE
Meal Direct live visual identity and product positioning, informed by the supplied master creative direction reference.
Prepared November 2026


How to use this library
These prompts are production briefs, not finished claims. Each one defines the message, composition, typography, imagery, copy, QR behavior, campus substitutions, format adaptations and final checks required to create a strong Meal Direct design. The system is designed to remain recognizably Meal Direct while changing its visual rhythm across 28 campaign needs.
1.Select the campaign prompt that matches the actual objective. Do not repurpose a recruitment, event, review or vendor prompt for a different claim.
2.Complete the required inputs with approved names, URLs, QR artwork, imagery and operational facts. Delete optional fields that cannot be verified.
3.Give the complete prompt and supplied assets to the designer or image generation workflow. Generate the background or photographic concept first when needed, then compose text, logo and QR code in layout software.
4.Create format specific layouts. Reflow the hierarchy for feed, story and print; do not squeeze one master into every shape.
5.Run the truth, readability, scan and production checks at the end of the selected prompt before release.
Campaign categories
Category	Prompts	Use
Launch and acquisition	01–09	Launch, anticipation, ordering, awareness, first use, referral, value, cravings and routine.
Marketplace growth	10–16	Vendor, ambassador, representative and delivery partner recruitment or features.
Product education and proof	17–20	Ordering, fulfillment, student feedback and real weekly selections.
Campus and print activation	21–28	Posters, QR cards, events, challenges, partners, flyers and packaging inserts.


Meal Direct brand and production system
Apply this system to every prompt unless the prompt gives a more specific instruction. It preserves the live Meal Direct identity while translating the supplied creative direction into a campus food context: bold designed typography, controlled asymmetry, realistic food and student life, restrained tactile detail, clear information hierarchy and one dominant action.
Brand palette
Role	Value	Application
Primary green	#0B6B4F	Main brand field, headline, CTA and high confidence signal.
Deep green	#074C39	Depth, dark panels, secondary emphasis and print contrast.
Mint	#BDE8D6	Supporting shapes, step markers and soft visual separation.
Pale green	#ECF7F2	Editorial background, quiet cards and paper fields.
Ink	#0F172A	Primary body text and near black contrast.
Slate	#475569	Secondary copy and metadata.
White	#FFFFFF	Clean space, reversed type and the required QR field.
Typography and voice
Use Outfit for display headlines and major numeric or step signals. Use Inter for body copy, CTAs, metadata and functional labels.
Favor short, direct headlines with purposeful line breaks. Use scale contrast rather than many decorative elements.
Write for Nigerian university students and campus food businesses in clear, natural English. Keep the tone useful, energetic and respectful; avoid forced slang and exaggerated hype.
Do not use absolute or unsupported language such as cheapest, guaranteed, always on time, available 24/7, instant delivery or everyone is ordering.
Logo handling
Use only the supplied official Meal Direct files. The square icon is suited to compact placements. The full lockup includes the mark, the lowercase Meal Direct wordmark and the FOOD. DELIVERED. DIRECT. tagline; give it enough size for the tagline to remain legible. Never redraw, recolor, stretch, crop, rotate, outline or generate the mark. If an image generator is involved, reserve a clean logo location and composite the genuine asset afterward.
QR code rules
Generate the destination outside the visual model, then composite the exact supplied QR artwork as a flat image. Never ask an image model to invent a scannable QR pattern.
Place the code on pure white with a quiet zone at least four modules wide. Keep photographs, texture, gradients, shadows, borders and decorative marks outside that zone.
Include a short human readable URL pointing to the same destination. Use the prompt specific campaign destination rather than defaulting every design to the ordering homepage.
Treat the dimensions in the prompts as starting points. Test the actual exported code on at least two phones, at intended print size and at realistic viewing distance.
University and campus flexibility
Keep {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}} and {{CAMPUS_NAME}} as independent editable text layers. Allow a two line university name at natural word breaks before reducing its size.
Reserve width for long names during initial composition. Do not solve overflow by compressing letterforms, using a narrow unreadable font or covering the hero image.
Never place a university crest or claim official endorsement unless the asset and approval are supplied for that exact campaign.


Truth, imagery and export standards
Meal Direct is presented on its live website as scheduled campus meal delivery: students select meals and delivery times, place or schedule orders, pay through the ordering process and receive meals through campus optimized fulfillment. Preserve that scheduled model. Do not visually or verbally convert it into an instant dispatch promise.
Facts that require campaign approval
Live status, launch date, event date, event venue and campus coverage.
Vendor identity, menu availability, meal photography, item names, quantities and prices.
Discounts, rewards, referral incentives, free delivery, first order offers and eligibility rules.
Student quotations, names, courses, portraits, ratings and permission to publish.
University or community partnerships, logos, spokespeople and the wording of the relationship.
Role requirements, compensation, commissions, work hours, equipment and application criteria.
Payment methods, refund rules, delivery windows, pickup points, live tracking and subscription availability for the named campus.
Photography direction
Prefer real, approved photography for named vendors, meals, students, staff, riders, events and partners. For general awareness concepts, use credible Nigerian campus contexts: natural skin tones, realistic food textures, clean but lived in hostel or study environments, practical meal packaging and believable daylight or warm indoor light. Avoid generic American campus cues, luxury restaurant staging, glossy plastic food, extra fingers, warped utensils, unreadable signage and visual claims that imply a real partnership.
Format system
Format	Size	Production rule
Feed	1080 × 1350 px	12 column grid, 64 px safe margin, strong 4:5 hierarchy.
Story	1080 × 1920 px	Reflow; protect the top and bottom 250 px from essential content.
Square	1080 × 1080 px	Remove optional support before reducing headline or QR size.
A3 poster	297 × 420 mm	3 mm bleed, minimum 12 mm internal safety, 300 ppi imagery.
A4 poster	210 × 297 mm	3 mm bleed, minimum 10–12 mm safety, proof at actual size.
A6 card	105 × 148 mm	3 mm bleed, minimum 6 mm safety, large scan target.
A7 insert	74 × 105 mm	3 mm bleed, minimum 5 mm safety, essential copy only.
Universal release checks
One second check: the message and intended action are immediately clear.
Thumbnail check: headline, hero subject, contrast and Meal Direct brand signal survive at 25% size.
Long name check: the longest approved university name fits without collision or awkward compression.
Fact check: every campus, vendor, event, menu, price, role, review, benefit and partnership statement has an approved source.
Scan check: the final exported QR opens the correct destination on at least two devices.
Print check: bleed, safety, color conversion, image resolution and QR scale are approved with the selected printer; export PDF/X-4 when requested by the printer.
Editability check: text, logo, campus, photograph, CTA and QR remain separate named layers in the source file.
Restraint check: remove 20% of decoration; keep the simpler version when hierarchy improves.

prompts.title: Campus Launch
prompts.requiredInputs: {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_URL}}  ·  {{QR_ASSET}}  ·  {{LOGO_PRIMARY}}  ·  Confirmed live status for this campus  ·  Approved representative food image or actual participating vendor meal photo
prompts.body:
Objective and publication gate
Create a distinctive Meal Direct campus-launch campaign announcing that ordering is genuinely live at {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}, {{CAMPUS_NAME}}. Address students who may be seeing Meal Direct for the first time. Communicate arrival first, appetizing meal discovery second, and the campus ordering action third. Use this version only after the campus page, participating availability and ordering status have been confirmed. If launch is still pending, switch to the Coming Soon brief. Do not infer launch status from the existence of a university name or a website.
Format and composition
Build a 1080 × 1350 px portrait master on a 12-column invisible grid with 64 px safe margins. Use an assertive green campaign field, an oversized left-aligned statement across the upper half, and one close-cropped meal photograph entering from the right at mid-height. Let the food overlap an empty area beside the type, never a letter required for reading. Reserve the lower quarter for the campus identity and scan panel. Create tension through the contrast between monumental type and a tactile, believable meal, with one clear diagonal of attention from headline to food to CTA.
Exact copy and information order
Set the headline exactly: “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}},\nwe’re live.” Set the supporting sentence: “Explore campus meals and choose an available delivery slot with Meal Direct.” Set the campus label: “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”. Set the primary CTA: “Scan to order”. Place {{CAMPUS_URL}} beneath the scan label as a readable fallback. Treat all double-brace fields as editable template tokens that must be replaced before publication. Do not add “official”, “exclusive”, “fastest”, “free delivery”, a launch date, a first-order discount, vendor names or a delivery-time promise unless separately supplied and approved.
Typography and identity
Use Outfit ExtraBold for the hero statement and Inter for support, campus information and CTA. Begin with a 104–126 px hero treatment, then adapt to the actual university name. A long university name may occupy two intentional lines; reduce its size modestly before changing the fixed CTA or QR dimensions. Keep “we’re live.” visually dominant without making the university feel incidental. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} near the upper-left safe edge as an intact supplied asset. Preserve its colors, aspect ratio and surrounding breathing room; never typeset a substitute wordmark or generate an approximation.
Color, food and material direction
Make #0B6B4F the dominant background, #074C39 a restrained shadow or lower information band, and white the headline color. Use #BDE8D6 for one small accent and #ECF7F2 for a supporting surface only when necessary. Keep the meal naturally colored and appetizing: distinct grains, believable sauce, realistic protein texture and controlled highlights. Use a supplied participating-vendor image when the meal is identifiable; otherwise use clearly representative food without vendor or availability attribution. Light from the upper left with a soft grounded shadow. Add fine paper grain only to empty color fields.
Campus and QR component
Create a reusable white scan tile in the lower-left or lower-center area, separated from the photograph. Composite {{QR_ASSET}} exactly, without redrawing modules, tinting, adding a logo inside, rounding modules or distorting perspective. Reserve a four-module quiet zone on every side. Start with a 260 px outer tile, then adjust according to actual code density and final scan tests; the sample size is not a guarantee. Keep the university and campus text on editable layers above the utility band. Ensure the QR destination and printed {{CAMPUS_URL}} lead to the same campus.
Adaptations and editable construction
Create a 1080 × 1920 story version by increasing vertical breathing room, moving the food into the middle third and keeping headline, campus and scan action in separate readable zones. Reflow the composition; do not stretch the feed artwork. Keep all essential content away from platform interface areas, checking the actual placement preview. Include separate layers for background, grain, food cutout, headline, support, campus name, official logo, QR and URL. Provide a text-free image plate for regeneration and an assembled reference artwork so the final accurate typography and assets can be placed in design software.
Exclusions and restraint
Exclude fireworks, confetti overload, fake campus seals, map pins implying unsupported coverage, crowds implying attendance, countdowns, app-store badges and fabricated phone interfaces. Do not use Sulva purple, its diagonal symbol, technology slogans or fake system codes. Avoid glossy three-dimensional letters, neon effects, excessive rounded cards and multiple competing meals. Keep the launch feeling confident and human through scale, food texture and clean spacing. Any decorative underline or arrow must direct attention to the actual ordering action; omit it if the hierarchy already works.
Delivery and review
Deliver clean, flat feed and story artwork, an editable master and high-quality sRGB previews. Label this as a launch template requiring live-status verification. Check the composition at approximately 25% scale: the university, “we’re live.” and the action should remain apparent. Proofread the substituted names, test long-name examples, confirm that no placeholder is visible, and scan the final exported code using more than one device. Verify the actual campus destination and available ordering flow. Remove any decorative element that competes with the announcement or makes the QR harder to locate.

prompts.title: Coming Soon
prompts.requiredInputs: {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_URL}}  ·  {{QR_ASSET}}  ·  {{LOGO_PRIMARY}}  ·  Confirmation that a campus arrival is planned  ·  Verified purpose of the campus landing page  ·  Optional approved launch date
prompts.body:
Objective and status
Create a Meal Direct coming-soon visual for a campus where arrival is planned but ordering has not yet been announced as live. Make students curious without implying that they can place an order today. The desired action is to visit the relevant campus page and learn what has actually been published there. Confirm that {{CAMPUS_URL}} exists and accurately supports that purpose. If it offers a verified notification form, a separate approved CTA may refer to updates; never imply an updates feature, waitlist or launch date that has not been supplied.
Editorial concept and geometry
Build a 1080 × 1350 px portrait using a 12-column grid and 64 px margins. Use a pale, tactile field with a huge typographic promise on the left and a tightly cropped plate on the right, partly obscured by a clean vertical paper panel. The reveal should suggest anticipation through composition, not through blurred or unappetizing food. Let approximately one-third of the meal remain visible, with its texture clearly recognizable. Position a small “COMING SOON” label above the headline and a restrained green utility strip across the bottom. Preserve an open middle-left area.
Exact visible copy
Set the small status label exactly: “COMING SOON”. Set the headline: “Something tasty\nis coming.” Set the supporting line: “Meal Direct is coming to {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}.” Add {{CAMPUS_NAME}} as a separate location label. Use the CTA: “Explore your campus page”. Put {{CAMPUS_URL}} under the code. Do not display an invented countdown or launch date. If a date is approved, add a small separate line using the actual supplied wording, with no time or timezone invented. Replace all template tokens before publication; remove optional information modules entirely when their facts are absent.
Typography and brand assets
Use Outfit Bold or ExtraBold for “Something tasty” at a starting size of 106 px, with “is coming.” slightly smaller or on a tightly controlled second line. Use Inter Medium for the coming-soon label and Inter Regular for context. Keep the university name large enough to establish relevance, allowing it to wrap across two lines within a stable text block. Place the supplied {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} at the upper-left or upper-right safe edge, whichever balances the plate crop. Use the actual asset unchanged and maintain generous clear space; do not build a logo from ordinary text.
Palette and image treatment
Use #ECF7F2 as the main field, #0B6B4F for the headline and lower utility strip, and #074C39 for small high-contrast text. Use #BDE8D6 only as a subtle panel or annotation accent. Keep the plate white and the food naturally colored. Choose a believable Nigerian campus meal scene with careful styling and soft side light; avoid implying that a named meal or vendor is confirmed. Use a representative visual only when actual launch-menu photography is unavailable. Add a gentle physical paper edge and faint grain, but keep the overall surface clean and the food in sharp focus.
Replaceable scan and campus module
Reserve a flat white QR module within the bottom band, approximately 240–280 px square as a starting point. Place {{QR_ASSET}} as the exact supplied artwork with a minimum four-module quiet zone. Never ask the image model to synthesize a scan pattern. Keep texture, paper folds, shadow and decorative elements outside the QR tile. Align the CTA and human-readable {{CAMPUS_URL}} beside or below it, with enough space for a longer campus route. Confirm both destinations match. Protect this module when changing universities; adjust text wrapping and photograph position before reducing scan size.
Variants and production layers
Rebuild for a 1080 × 1920 story with the headline in the upper third, an enlarged partial food reveal through the middle, and the campus/QR block lower down within the platform’s tested safe region. An approved date may occupy a small caption line, never replace the campus name or QR label. Separate the reveal panel from the food image so its crop can change without regenerating the entire composition. Maintain editable layers for every text field, brand asset and code. Deliver a clean background image plate plus a final assembled layout; do not claim editable type from a flattened AI image.
Negative direction and truth rules
Avoid “order now”, “we’re live”, instant-delivery promises, 24/7 claims, fake push notifications, app launch badges, reward vouchers and manufactured scarcity. Do not suggest that the university officially sponsors the service. Do not add institutional logos unless specifically provided and authorized for the campaign. Avoid mystery boxes, excessive question marks, neon glows and generic teaser smoke. The concept should feel like an appetizing editorial reveal from a useful campus brand. Retain the source reference’s hierarchy and restraint while using Meal Direct’s green identity throughout.
Final checks and output
Export feed and story previews in sRGB at their stated dimensions and include the editable composition. Check that the coming-soon status is immediately understood and never contradicted by the CTA. Review the actual landing-page purpose, the spelling of the university and campus, and the behavior of long names. Scan the exported QR at realistic viewing size and on multiple devices. At quarter scale, the headline, planned-arrival status and campus relevance must remain clear. If a verified date was supplied, check it again before distribution; otherwise keep the design deliberately date-free.

prompts.title: Order Now
prompts.requiredInputs: {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_URL}}  ·  {{QR_ASSET}}  ·  {{LOGO_PRIMARY}}  ·  Confirmed live campus ordering page  ·  Approved representative meal image or verified available meal photo
prompts.body:
Conversion objective
Create a Meal Direct campaign that turns a student’s interest into a visit to the campus ordering page. The message should make choosing the next meal feel simple and appetizing while accurately reflecting scheduled delivery. Confirm that ordering is available for {{CAMPUS_NAME}} before using this execution. The action is to browse actual meals, select an available delivery slot and complete the real ordering flow. Do not turn “Order Now” into an assertion that food arrives immediately. Treat timing, fees and availability as information the live page supplies.
Hero composition
Create a 1080 × 1350 px feed artwork on a 12-column grid with 64 px safe margins. Use a large overhead food photograph occupying the upper-right two-thirds, cropped boldly so the meal feels close and inviting. Place a solid green vertical text panel over the left third with the headline stacked into short readable lines. Let a single plate edge cross behind the panel boundary without covering text. Use the bottom quarter as a calm pale utility shelf containing the campus identification and scan action. Keep the visual path direct: craving, choice, scan.
Exact copy
Set the headline: “Choose your\nnext meal.” Set a short supporting line: “Explore available meals and choose a delivery slot that works for you.” Use the location line: “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}} · {{CAMPUS_NAME}}”, allowing a line break instead of forcing both onto one line. Set the CTA exactly: “Scan to order”. Put {{CAMPUS_URL}} below it. Do not include a price, delivery duration, discount, “no fees”, a sellout warning or a vendor name by default. These are editable template fields, not permission to fabricate missing facts. Replace every visible placeholder before the artwork is published.
Type and logo hierarchy
Use Outfit ExtraBold for the headline, starting at 106–118 px with compact line spacing. Use Inter for the supporting sentence and campus details at a clearly readable 28–34 px starting range. Use a confident Inter Semibold CTA without adding a second action button. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} on a clean area near the upper margin, using the approved original asset with preserved aspect ratio and color. If it needs a contrasting backing, use a quiet white panel rather than recoloring the logo. Long university names may wrap across two lines; keep the scan component fixed.
Food art direction and palette
Show one compelling, plausible meal with recognizably real grains, vegetables or sauce and carefully controlled oily highlights. Prefer an actual approved available-meal photograph; otherwise use a generic representative meal without naming it as a current listing. Keep portions believable and avoid adding extra proteins that misrepresent an actual item. Light from one side to reveal texture, with a matte tabletop and soft natural shadows. Use #0B6B4F for the headline panel, white type, #ECF7F2 for the utility shelf, #074C39 for supporting text and a small #BDE8D6 accent. Avoid food-color filters.
QR utility panel
Reserve a white square tile of about 260 px outer size as an initial layout reference. Place the exact supplied {{QR_ASSET}} inside it and preserve at least four modules of quiet zone on every side. Keep the code square, sharp and unobstructed; do not add decorative dots, center icons, texture or perspective. The image generator should leave this area blank for accurate composition. Pair it with “Scan to order” and the human-readable {{CAMPUS_URL}}. Confirm that the visible link and code share the intended campus destination. Increase the tile if code density or real-world testing requires it.
Adaptations and editable delivery
For a 1080 × 1920 story, convert the narrow text panel into a wide upper headline block, move the meal into the central area and retain a separate campus/QR utility area below. Preserve sufficient platform-safe space above and below the useful content. A compact square adaptation may reduce supporting copy, but must retain the university, order action and readable link. Supply separate layers for food, solid fields, text, logo, code and route. Deliver a clean photo plate and assembled reference alongside the editable master so branding and text accuracy do not depend on generative rendering.
What to exclude
Do not show a fictional checkout, fabricated customer count, invented five-star rating, fake bestseller badge, crossed-out price or unsupported delivery map. Avoid multiple CTAs such as “download”, “follow”, “join” and “order” competing on the same canvas. Exclude generic floating phone screens, neon outlines, overly glossy sauce, duplicate utensils and implausible food anatomy. Do not imply that the campus endorses the service. Keep decoration minimal: one purposeful line or small arrow may guide toward the scan panel, but the food and headline must remain the only major attention drivers.
Export and acceptance
Export clean sRGB feed and story artwork and retain the editable layout. Test at quarter scale for an immediately recognizable meal, headline and order action. Check that the supporting copy explicitly allows scheduled delivery rather than promising immediate arrival. Verify all substituted names and the actual campus ordering route. Test the QR in the final exports on multiple devices, including a smaller on-screen display. Confirm no placeholder, fictional offer or unavailable menu claim remains. If actual meal photography was used, confirm that its visual presentation accurately represents the item being promoted.

prompts.title: Campus Awareness
prompts.requiredInputs: {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_URL}}  ·  {{QR_ASSET}}  ·  {{LOGO_PRIMARY}}  ·  Confirmed campus service status  ·  Approved representative meal photo
prompts.body:
Audience and core message
Design an introductory Meal Direct graphic for students who do not yet know what the service does. Explain that Meal Direct connects them with campus meal options and scheduled delivery, then point them toward the relevant campus page. Make the message welcoming and easy to understand without assuming familiarity with the brand, local vendors or the ordering process. Publish a live-service version only where the campus service is confirmed. Avoid broad claims about all restaurants, every hostel, campus-wide coverage or instant fulfillment.
Composition and hierarchy
Use a 1080 × 1350 px portrait canvas, a 12-column grid and 64 px safe margins. Build an editorial explanation with three clear horizontal zones: a large introductory headline in the upper quarter, a central illustrated journey across three simple modules, and a bottom campus/QR utility band. Place one cropped meal photograph beside the introduction rather than repeating food in every module. Connect the modules with restrained arrows so the reading order is obvious. Maintain open space around the headline and use unequal scale to prevent a generic dashboard appearance.
Exact visible wording
Set the headline: “Meet Meal Direct.” Set the secondary statement: “Meals for campus life.” Use the body: “Discover campus food options and order for an available delivery slot.” Label the three explanation modules: “Explore menus”, “Choose your meal and slot”, and “Complete your order”. Add “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}” and “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}” as separate location lines. Set the CTA: “Explore your campus page”, followed by {{CAMPUS_URL}}. Keep these words exact unless approved local product information requires a correction. Replace all double-brace tokens before publication.
Type and brand placement
Use Outfit ExtraBold for the headline at approximately 98–110 px, Outfit Semibold for module labels and Inter for the body and utility text. Keep the three module labels large enough to survive mobile viewing, using short wraps rather than compressed tracking. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} in the top-left safe region or in a reserved signature area above the footer. Preserve the supplied logo exactly. Allow the university name to wrap over two lines and the campus line to remain separate; never shrink the whole artwork to accommodate a longer location.
Color, objects and diagram treatment
Use white or #F8FAFC as the base, #0F172A for main text, #0B6B4F for the primary headline accent and CTA, and #ECF7F2 for the diagram area. Use #BDE8D6 sparingly for one step marker. The supporting objects can be a real menu fragment, a simple plate silhouette and a clear confirmation check, drawn in one consistent line style. Do not fabricate readable menu items, prices or an actual checkout screen. Give the meal photograph natural light, realistic food texture and a clean crop. Keep any background grain extremely subtle.
QR and replacement system
Reserve a white QR tile starting at 260 px outer size, leaving a clear four-module quiet zone around {{QR_ASSET}}. Composite the actual code after image generation; do not generate a decorative stand-in. Pair it with the CTA and readable {{CAMPUS_URL}}, confirming that both destinations match. Keep QR, logo, names, body and module labels independently editable. The bottom band should expand vertically when a university name wraps. Move supporting imagery before reducing the code. Test actual scan performance instead of treating the starting pixel size as a universal minimum.
Story and print adaptations
Reflow the journey into a vertical sequence for a 1080 × 1920 story: introduction, three short steps, then campus and scan action. Keep all essential content within the platform’s verified visible region. If adapting to an introductory A4 handout, rebuild using a generous print-safe area, printer-confirmed bleed and suitable QR dimensions for the real viewing distance. Do not merely scale down the social artwork. Deliver separate image and diagram assets, an editable layout, and assembled previews with real type and the actual supplied logo and code.
Exclusions
Avoid making this introduction look like a technical manual, app-install advertisement or restaurant menu. Exclude fictional mobile interfaces, download badges, payment-method claims, unsupported delivery estimates and statements about all-campus availability. Do not add institutional crests or claim a university partnership. Avoid too many icon styles, floating cards, clip-art riders and stacks of food photographs. Transfer the reference document’s clear hierarchy, disciplined asymmetry and material restraint into Meal Direct’s identity; exclude its purple palette, Sulva slogans and decorative technical terminology.
Completion checks
Deliver sRGB feed and story files plus the editable master. Ask whether someone new to campus could explain Meal Direct’s purpose after a brief look. At quarter size, the brand introduction and action must remain understandable. Check the three-step description against the current campus flow and remove any unsupported feature. Proofread university and campus names, confirm no template field remains, and test the exact exported QR on multiple devices. Verify that the campus destination actually explains or provides the service promised by the artwork.

prompts.title: First Order
prompts.requiredInputs: {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_URL}}  ·  {{QR_ASSET}}  ·  {{LOGO_PRIMARY}}  ·  Confirmed live ordering destination  ·  Approved lifestyle or representative food image
prompts.body:
Intention and audience
Create a warm Meal Direct first-order visual for students who are interested but have not ordered before. Make the experience feel approachable through a clear starting point and a calm, useful explanation. The campaign should welcome a new user without suggesting that a discount, voucher, free item or waived fee exists. Confirm that the campus ordering flow is live. Keep the promise limited to discovering meals and following the available ordering process; do not guarantee simplicity through invented one-tap checkout or unsupported account-free ordering.
Composition concept
Build a 1080 × 1350 px portrait composition using a 12-column grid and 64 px margins. Create a welcoming editorial card on a softly lit study-table scene: the card holds the main words, while a believable meal and a student’s hand or notebook appear as secondary cropped context near opposite edges. Keep the card front-facing so text can be composited cleanly. Allocate approximately the upper half to the welcome, a short middle row to the next steps, and a stable lower-right area to the scan panel. Leave generous breathing room.
Exact visible copy
Use a small introductory label: “FIRST TIME HERE?” Set the main headline: “Your first order\nstarts here.” Use the body: “Browse campus meals, choose an available delivery slot, and follow checkout to place your order.” Add the location as “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}” and “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”. Set the CTA: “Explore your first order”. Display {{CAMPUS_URL}} clearly beneath it. Optionally emphasize the words “Browse”, “Choose” and “Order” in the layout without adding unsupported steps. Replace every variable with actual campus information before publishing; omit any optional detail that cannot be confirmed.
Typography and logo
Use Outfit Bold for the headline, starting at 100–112 px with friendly, confident spacing. Keep all essential headline letters intact and avoid decorative cropping. Use Inter for the body, labels, campus details and CTA, with enough line height to feel welcoming. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} above the headline or in a quiet upper corner, using the supplied asset unchanged. Keep a clear area around it. A long university name may wrap to two lines; reduce its font slightly only after giving the text block more height. Never compromise the QR to fit the name.
Palette and photographic details
Use #F8FAFC or white for the welcome card, #ECF7F2 for the surrounding field, #0B6B4F for the headline and CTA, and #1E293B for body text. Add #BDE8D6 as a subtle edge or small underline. Show a realistic student setting with ordinary notebook paper, a simple pen and a credible meal container or plate. Use natural side light, gentle shadows and truthful food proportions. Do not show a celebratory gift box, a wallet full of money, branded university stationery or a phone screen with invented transactional information.
Scan tile and editable fields
Give {{QR_ASSET}} a clean, square white tile beginning around 260 px outer size. Preserve the actual code without artistic transformation and retain at least four modules of quiet zone. The generator must leave the space available for accurate composition. Place the CTA beside or above the code and the readable {{CAMPUS_URL}} below. Confirm that the two routes match and lead to the correct campus. Keep all names, copy, logo and code as editable layers. Re-test scanning after any resize or replacement because QR density varies across campus links.
Format adaptations
For the 1080 × 1920 story version, use a taller welcome card with the meal image beneath the headline and a distinct scan block lower down. Maintain safe clearance from platform controls. For a small first-order insert, shorten the body before reducing text below comfortable reading size; retain the welcome, university, CTA and link. Provide the photo background as a separate image plate, editable text and accurate brand/QR layers, plus a flat assembled preview. Keep the final graphic clean enough to function without the photographed table context if a minimal variant is needed.
Avoid and verify
Exclude “welcome discount”, “free first meal”, “first delivery on us”, coupon shapes, crossed-out prices and reward icons. Do not imply eligibility rules or service benefits that have not been supplied. Avoid excessive confetti, childish stickers, crowded instructional bubbles and false reassurance such as guaranteed delivery. Keep the mood warm through human detail and readable information rather than exaggerated smiling faces. Use Meal Direct’s own logo and palette throughout; do not import Sulva’s visual symbols or slogans. Do not imply an institutional endorsement.
Export and quality review
Deliver sRGB feed and story artwork plus the editable master. Check that a first-time user can identify where to begin without mistaking the design for a promotional offer. Review the copy against the live ordering flow and verify the scheduled-delivery language. Test the longest expected university name, confirm all placeholders are replaced, and scan the final QR from multiple devices. At 25% scale, the welcome, campus relevance and scan action must remain recognizable. Confirm that any visible food is representative or accurately sourced from a verified available item.

prompts.title: Referral
prompts.requiredInputs: {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_URL}}  ·  {{QR_ASSET}}  ·  {{LOGO_PRIMARY}}  ·  Confirmed shareable campus landing page  ·  Approved student lifestyle photo, if used
prompts.body:
Sharing objective
Create a Meal Direct referral-awareness visual that encourages students to share the campus link with friends. Treat referral here as a simple community action, not as a reward scheme. The graphic must not imply money, meal credits, referral codes, points, tracking dashboards or guaranteed benefits unless separately verified. The intended behavior is to open {{CAMPUS_URL}}, copy or share that actual link through the student’s preferred channel, and help another student discover the service. Confirm the landing page and campus identity before publication.
Distinctive composition
Use a 1080 × 1350 px portrait master with a 12-column grid and 64 px margins. Build an asymmetrical two-part composition: an authentic cropped photograph of two students sharing a phone or meal moment across the upper-right area, and a large statement rising from the lower-left. Add a single continuous green line that moves from the campus-link label toward the scan module, suggesting connection without becoming a fake interface. Reserve the lower quarter for a stable campus/QR strip. Leave enough negative space that the headline does not compete with faces.
Exact copy and action
Set the headline: “Good food links\nare worth sharing.” Set the body: “Share your Meal Direct campus link with a friend at {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}.” Use a small label: “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”. Set the CTA: “Scan. Open. Share.” Place {{CAMPUS_URL}} as a prominent readable route near the code. Do not invent a promotional hashtag, referral code or incentive. If the website lacks a dedicated share button, the design must still make sense as ordinary browser-link sharing. Replace every visible template token before publication and keep only confirmed campus information.
Typography and brand identity
Use Outfit ExtraBold for the headline, beginning around 100–114 px and adjusting breaks to preserve rhythm. Use Inter for the body and the link, with the URL large enough to copy manually if needed. Keep the dot-separated CTA readable as three short actions rather than three tiny badges. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} in a clean corner away from faces and the code. Use the actual asset with its native proportions and colors. Allow long university names two lines within the body block, and retain an independent campus label rather than crowding both into the headline.
Color and human photography
Use a white or #ECF7F2 base, #0B6B4F for the headline and connecting line, #074C39 for small labels and #1E293B for body text. Let #BDE8D6 support one subtle panel behind the human photograph. Show believable student interaction with natural expressions and ordinary campus surroundings, avoiding identifiable institutional branding or staged corporate handshakes. If a phone screen is visible, keep it non-readable or composite an approved real screenshot. Do not fabricate personal messages, names, account details or notifications. Use soft daylight and restrained documentary texture.
QR and link module
Reserve a white QR tile starting at 260 px outer size and composite {{QR_ASSET}} exactly. Maintain at least a four-module quiet zone, with no connecting line, texture or shadow crossing it. Never generate an imitation QR. Place the readable {{CAMPUS_URL}} immediately beside or beneath the scan instruction. Verify that the code and visible URL resolve to the same shareable campus page. The module should remain intact across university variants; let the surrounding headline and photo crop adapt. Test scanning on the final artwork rather than assuming that a sample pixel size guarantees success.
Story and share-card variants
Reflow into a 1080 × 1920 story with the human photograph across the middle, the headline above and the campus/QR block below, within checked platform-safe boundaries. Create an optional minimal share-card version using the headline, campus name, link, logo and code without the photograph. Keep the same hierarchy across variants while allowing different crops. Supply editable layers for every name and route, the exact logo and QR, and the line motif. Provide a separate photo plate and assembled preview so final text does not depend on generated lettering.
Negative direction
Exclude cash, gift boxes, coins, coupon shapes, leaderboard graphics, points counters, “earn”, “get rewarded” and “invite and win”. Avoid fake chat bubbles suggesting a real student recommendation. Do not include testimonials or endorsement language unless genuine statements are supplied with permission. Keep the connection metaphor simple; do not surround the design with a web of nodes, many arrows or floating profile circles. Use a relatable, useful campus tone rather than aggressive viral marketing. Exclude Sulva’s purple, technology labels and brand geometry.
Review and deliverables
Deliver feed and story previews in sRGB plus the editable master. Verify that the first impression is “share this campus link”, with no expectation of a financial reward. Check university spelling, campus accuracy and route consistency; remove all placeholders before publication. Test the final code on multiple devices and confirm it opens a page that can actually be shared. At quarter scale, keep the headline, brand and action readable. Check any depicted people and screenshots for necessary usage permission and ensure no invented personal conversation is presented as evidence.

prompts.title: Student Value
prompts.requiredInputs: {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_URL}}  ·  {{QR_ASSET}}  ·  {{LOGO_PRIMARY}}  ·  Optional verified campus pricing or grouped-delivery information  ·  Approved representative meal photograph
prompts.body:
Objective and claim boundary
Create a Meal Direct student-value design for {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}, {{CAMPUS_NAME}} that presents planned meal ordering as a useful way to make campus food decisions with more intention. Communicate practical value through clarity, choice and scheduling rather than through an unverified cheapness claim. The intended action is to explore available campus meals through {{CAMPUS_URL}}. Use an approved price, delivery-fee statement or savings comparison only when it is supplied for the exact campus and time period. Do not promise that Meal Direct is always the cheapest option, prevents overspending, fits every budget or guarantees a particular saving.
Visual concept and format
Build a 1080 × 1350 px portrait master on an invisible 12-column grid with 64 px safe margins. Use an editorial meal-planning concept: a realistic overhead desk or hostel-table scene combines one appealing packaged meal, a notebook with a simple non-monetary weekly meal rhythm and a phone-sized empty interface frame reserved for approved ordering artwork. Keep the upper-left third open for a decisive headline. Use exact alignment for labels and a slightly offset meal crop to keep the scene human. The visual should imply thoughtful planning, not financial anxiety, coupon hunting or a luxury dining experience.
Exact visible copy
Set the headline exactly: “Plan your meals.
Keep campus moving.” Use the supporting line: “Explore available campus meals and choose a delivery slot that works with your day.” Add the label “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}} / {{CAMPUS_NAME}}”. Set the CTA to “Scan to explore meals” and place {{CAMPUS_URL}} beneath the code. If verified campus value information is supplied, add it as one factual line in the form {{APPROVED_VALUE_FACT}}; otherwise remove that module completely. Do not add a currency amount, percentage, ‘student price’, subscription saving, free-delivery claim or comparison with another service unless each detail is approved.
Typography and identity
Use Outfit ExtraBold for the headline, beginning around 100–116 px, with a strong two-line break and tight but readable leading. Use Inter Medium for the campus label and CTA, and Inter Regular at 29–33 px for support. Make ‘Plan your meals.’ the first reading point and ‘Keep campus moving.’ the second. Allow {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}} to wrap to two intentional lines within a dedicated width; reduce its label size only to a comfortable minimum before altering the layout. Composite the approved {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} asset unchanged in a quiet top corner. Keep clear space around it and never recreate its icon or tagline with generated graphics.
Color, imagery and material direction
Use #ECF7F2 as the main editorial paper field, #0B6B4F for the headline and CTA, #074C39 for the bottom utility band, #BDE8D6 for one planning marker, white for the QR field and #0F172A for body text. Photograph the meal from approximately 70–80 degrees with soft window light, controlled shadows and credible packaging. Include familiar study objects sparingly: one notebook, pen and neutral phone prop. Do not show cash piles, empty wallets, price-tag explosions or distressed students. Apply very fine paper grain only to empty background areas; keep food, approved screen content and scan components crisp.
Flexible value and QR modules
Create two independent editable modules: a campus identity block and a white QR block. The campus block must accommodate a two-line university name and a one-line campus name without overlapping the image. The scan tile should begin around 260 px square including a quiet zone at least four modules wide, then be adjusted after testing the actual code density. Composite {{QR_ASSET}} exactly; do not recolor, round, crop, skew or generate its modules. Ensure the short URL and QR resolve to the same campus destination. If the URL, QR or approved campus page is missing, retain blank production slots and do not issue a publish-ready export.
Adaptations and construction
For 1080 × 1920 story, place the headline in the upper safe zone, the overhead meal-planning scene in the middle, and the CTA plus scan tile in the lower usable third, keeping essential content outside the top and bottom 250 px interface areas. For a square post, remove the optional approved-value fact before reducing the headline or QR. Build separate named layers for background, texture, meal, planning objects, headline, support, campus, optional fact, logo, QR and URL. Provide a text-free image plate as well as the complete layout so accurate type and brand assets can be composited after image generation.
Exclusions and integrity
Exclude sale stickers, discount bursts, coins, calculators, crossed-out prices, fabricated app screens, unapproved meal plans and any visual that equates student value with poor-quality food. Avoid the words cheap, cheapest, save, guaranteed, unlimited or free unless an approved campus-specific offer legally supports them. Do not suggest university endorsement with a crest or official color system. Do not import Sulva purple, technical diagrams or software codes. Keep the piece useful and optimistic through composition, meal quality and direct language; no decorative element may compete with the actual campus action.
Delivery and review
Deliver editable feed, story and requested print masters with separate text, photograph, campus, logo, optional fact and QR layers; export clean sRGB previews. Name files MD_07_Student_Value_{{CAMPUS_NAME}}_[format]. Check at 25% scale that the planning message, Meal Direct identity and scan action remain obvious. Test a long university name, inspect food realism and verify every displayed value fact against the approved source. Scan the final export on at least two devices. Remove any monetary or comparative implication that cannot be substantiated, and simplify the desk scene if it distracts from the meal and CTA.

prompts.title: Cravings
prompts.requiredInputs: {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_URL}}  ·  {{QR_ASSET}}  ·  {{LOGO_PRIMARY}}  ·  {{APPROVED_CATEGORIES}}  ·  Approved representative or actual menu imagery  ·  Optional verified vendor and item names
prompts.body:
Objective and availability gate
Create a high-appetite Meal Direct cravings campaign for students at {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}, {{CAMPUS_NAME}}. Lead with the feeling of deciding what to eat, then direct the viewer to browse what is actually available for the campus. The action is discovery, not a promise that every pictured meal can be ordered at all times. Use named categories, dishes, vendors, prices and availability labels only when the current campus listing has been checked. When approved category data is absent, keep the copy general and use representative food photography without naming or attributing the meal.
Composition and appetite concept
Build a 1080 × 1350 px portrait master with a 12-column grid and 64 px safe margins. Use a three-panel editorial crop rather than a conventional restaurant grid: one dominant meal fills roughly 55% of the frame, two narrow supporting crops suggest alternative appetites, and a solid green statement field occupies the upper-left. Let the dominant plate break one grid line but keep all food edges intentional and believable. Position the scan action in a calm lower corner. The reading order should be craving question, hero meal, category signals, then campus destination. Use only one dominant dish so the layout feels curated rather than like a crowded menu.
Exact copy and category behavior
Set the headline exactly: “What are you
craving today?” Set the support line: “Browse what’s available around {{CAMPUS_NAME}}.” Add a small campus label: “Meal Direct at {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}”. Set the CTA: “Scan to discover meals” and print {{CAMPUS_URL}} as the fallback. If {{APPROVED_CATEGORIES}} is provided, show no more than three concise category labels, preserving the approved wording and current availability. If a category cannot be verified, remove it. Never fabricate a dish name, vendor, price, portion size, dietary label, bestseller status, preparation method or stock message.
Typography and brand placement
Use Outfit ExtraBold for the question at approximately 104–122 px, with strong contrast and an architectural two-line break. Use Inter SemiBold for category labels and CTA, and Inter Regular at 28–32 px for the support line. Keep the question readable over a plain field rather than complex food. Allow the university label to wrap to two lines within its own module; never compress or track it tightly to force a fit. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} on a clean brand field, using the approved icon for compact placements or the full lockup only when its wordmark and tagline can remain legible. Do not recolor or redraw it.
Food photography and palette
Use #0B6B4F and #074C39 for statement fields, #ECF7F2 for one quiet label surface, #BDE8D6 for category markers, white for primary type and QR, and #0F172A for dark copy. Style food with realistic moisture, grains, sauce, vegetables and protein texture; preserve natural portion proportions and clean packaging. Use warm directional light with soft side shadows and accurate plate edges. For real vendor promotion, use approved current meal photography. For generic discovery, avoid recognizable branding and show the images as representative. Exclude plastic shine, impossible garnishes, repeated food textures, floating cutlery and exaggerated steam.
QR and modular campus fields
Reserve a flat white scan tile approximately 250–270 px square, including a quiet zone of at least four modules, separated from food detail and texture. Place {{QR_ASSET}} without stylization, perspective, cropping, transparency or embedded decorative logo. Encode and verify {{CAMPUS_URL}} or the approved meal-discovery route for that campus. Keep the category labels, university name, campus name, support text and URL as individual editable layers. Design the name block for a two-line university and one-line campus. If the approved campus route changes, update both QR and printed URL together; if either is missing, withhold final publication artwork.
Adaptations and image-generation workflow
For story, recompose the dominant dish into the middle half, hold the headline in the upper safe area and place category labels plus scan action in the lower usable area outside the bottom interface zone. For square, retain the hero meal and question; remove secondary crops before shrinking text. Generate or retouch food plates without readable text, logo or QR, then assemble the final artwork in design software using exact typography and assets. Maintain separate layers for each food crop, color field, question, support, categories, campus, logo, QR and URL so new university versions do not require re-generating the food scene.
Specific exclusions
Exclude unverified category carousels, fake search interfaces, delivery timers, ‘available now’ badges, order counts, five-star ratings, vendor logos and promotional pricing. Do not claim late-night, breakfast, lunch or dinner availability unless that category is verified for the campus and publication period. Avoid a chaotic food collage, unrelated stock meals, hyper-saturated color, flames, neon restaurant motifs and cartoon hunger icons. Do not use a university crest without approval. The final work should feel appetizing and immediate in emotion while remaining accurate about what students can discover after scanning.
Delivery and review
Deliver editable 4:5 and story masters, high-quality sRGB exports and any requested print adaptation with named image, copy, category, campus, logo and QR layers. Name files MD_08_Cravings_{{CAMPUS_NAME}}_[format]. Review at full size for food realism and at 25% for question, hero dish and action. Confirm every named item and category against the campus page immediately before publishing. Test the final code on at least two devices, confirm the printed route and scan destination match, and remove one supporting image if the composition feels like a menu catalogue rather than one clear craving prompt.

prompts.title: Campus Routine
prompts.requiredInputs: {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_NAME}}  ·  {{CAMPUS_URL}}  ·  {{QR_ASSET}}  ·  {{LOGO_PRIMARY}}  ·  {{APPROVED_DELIVERY_WINDOWS}}  ·  Approved campus lifestyle photograph  ·  Optional approved ordering screen
prompts.body:
Objective and operational boundary
Create a Meal Direct campus-routine design for {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}, {{CAMPUS_NAME}} that connects planning a meal with a real student day: lectures, reading, group work or an evening study session. Present Meal Direct as a scheduled option students can consider around their timetable. Do not claim that delivery operates during every lecture break, overnight, on demand or at any named hour unless the relevant campus windows are supplied and current. The single action is to view actual availability through {{CAMPUS_URL}} and choose from the options shown there.
Documentary concept and composition
Build a 1080 × 1350 px portrait master on a 12-column grid with 64 px safe margins. Use a documentary scene rather than a promotional pose: a Nigerian student at a library desk, study corner or hostel table transitions from notes or laptop work to an arriving packaged meal. Crop the person naturally at the shoulder or hands, preserving accurate anatomy and avoiding a staged thumbs-up. Place a vertical sequence of three small time-of-day or activity labels along one edge, and keep a generous solid field for the headline. The meal, student gesture and CTA should form one clear triangular reading path.
Exact copy and optional windows
Set the headline exactly: “Your day is full.
Plan the meal.” Set the supporting sentence: “Check available meals and delivery slots for {{CAMPUS_NAME}}.” Add the campus line: “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}”. Set the CTA: “Scan to plan your order” and show {{CAMPUS_URL}} below it. Use the small routine labels “LECTURES”, “STUDY” and “EVENING” as contexts, not delivery promises. If {{APPROVED_DELIVERY_WINDOWS}} is supplied, place the exact approved wording in a separate clearly labeled availability module. Never convert ‘evening’ into late-night or 24/7 delivery, and never invent times from the photograph.
Typography and brand system
Use Outfit ExtraBold for the two-line headline at approximately 100–118 px and Inter for all functional copy. Let ‘Plan the meal.’ carry the strongest green or white contrast. Set routine labels in small uppercase Inter SemiBold with generous tracking, using one consistent alignment. Preserve enough width for a two-line {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}} and test a long-name version before locking the composition. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} as a genuine supplied layer on a clean field, never over the student’s face, hands or the meal. Use the full lockup only when its small tagline remains readable; otherwise use the approved compact icon with a separate editable Meal Direct text label.
Color, light and realism
Use #ECF7F2 as the primary editorial field, #0B6B4F for the main statement and CTA, #074C39 for a lower utility band, #BDE8D6 for routine markers, #0F172A for body type and white for the QR surface. Light the scene with believable late-afternoon window light or warm study light, maintaining natural skin tone and food color. Include only purposeful campus objects: notebooks, one laptop, pen, bag and packaged meal. Keep the environment recognizable but not institution-specific unless an approved location photograph is used. Apply subtle grain to empty fields, never to faces, food, screens or QR.
Availability, campus and scan modules
Keep the campus name, university name, optional windows, ordering route and QR in separate reusable modules. Reserve a white 250–270 px scan tile including a four-module quiet zone; composite {{QR_ASSET}} exactly with no tint, rounding, logo insertion, perspective or image-model regeneration. The code and printed {{CAMPUS_URL}} must lead to the same campus ordering or availability page. Treat the sample dimensions as a starting point and validate the actual code. If operational windows are unavailable, remove the entire window module instead of filling it with generic breakfast, lunch, dinner or night labels. Do not publish with a placeholder URL or QR.
Responsive adaptations and construction
For story, expand the documentary photograph vertically in the middle, keep the headline within the upper usable zone and place scan action below the image but above the lower 250 px interface area. Stack the three routine labels along the left or turn them into one horizontal line without changing their meaning. For square, keep one student activity and remove optional time-window detail before reducing type. Maintain independent layers for photograph, background, routine labels, headline, campus, approved windows, logo, QR and URL. Provide a text-free photo plate so university and schedule versions can be produced without generating new people.
Exclusions and representation
Exclude alarm clocks promising exact arrival, countdown timers, night-sky graphics, 24/7 badges, instant-delivery language, fictional timetables, unapproved faculty names and crowds of identical students. Avoid stereotypes of exhausted or financially distressed students, excessive coffee, messy food or unhealthy all-night study. Do not imply that studying requires ordering food. Exclude fake app tracking, invented riders, university crests and Sulva technology motifs. Keep the photograph observational, inclusive and locally credible. The design should connect to routine through human context and clear planning language rather than a false operational guarantee.
Delivery and review
Deliver editable feed and story masters with sRGB exports and separate documentary image, type, campus, availability, logo, QR and URL layers. Name files MD_09_Campus_Routine_{{CAMPUS_NAME}}_[format]. Check the one-second reading order, 25% headline clarity, long-name fit and natural treatment of the student. Verify any displayed delivery window against current campus operations, and scan the final code on at least two devices. Confirm that no routine label can be mistaken for a service hour. Remove decorative objects or labels if the student, meal and planning action do not remain the three strongest elements.

prompts.title: Vendor Recruitment
prompts.body:
Objective and publication conditions
Create a Meal Direct vendor recruitment campaign for food businesses serving {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}} and {{CAMPUS_NAME}}. Communicate one message: explore joining Meal Direct for this campus. Make the application route the only primary action. Publish only after the campus partnership intake, eligible business types, application destination and actual operating model are approved. Describe this as an invitation to apply; do not imply that every applicant will be accepted, that a vendor is already participating, or that campus coverage is already live.
Canvas and composition
Build a 1080 × 1350 px portrait master on an invisible 12-column grid, with 64 px safe margins and 24 px gutters. Use an editorial split: a pale upper statement field occupying approximately 44% of the canvas, an authentic preparation photograph across the middle 32%, and a disciplined application strip below. Offset the photograph by one grid column to create controlled asymmetry. Keep the headline first, the food-business context second and the application action third. Avoid placing important text over food or hands.
Brand and typography
Use #ECF7F2 for the main paper field, #0B6B4F for the headline and application band, #074C39 for secondary emphasis, #BDE8D6 for one supporting label, and white for reversed CTA text. Set the headline in Outfit Bold at approximately 88–104 px; use Inter for body copy at 30–34 px and labels at 22–26 px. Composite the exact {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} asset from the approved /logofull.png or /logo.png file; preserve its proportions, official colors and clear space. Place full /logofull.png on white at a size that preserves its embedded tagline; use approved /logo.png with separate Meal Direct text for narrow placements.
Photography and material treatment
Use {{APPROVED_VENDOR_PHOTO}} when an actual participating or prospective business has authorized the image. Show a credible food-preparation moment: a clean counter, a carefully packed meal, natural hands and practical kitchen context. Use a 50 mm-equivalent viewpoint, soft side lighting and believable contact shadows. When an approved documentary photo is unavailable, create a clearly illustrative close-up of unbranded food packaging without people, business signage or implied endorsement. Apply only restrained paper grain to the background; protect food detail and functional modules.
Complete visible copy
Set the main headline exactly as “Serve your campus.” and the supporting invitation as “Explore becoming a Meal Direct vendor.” Place “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}” and “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}” together in a small campus module. Include a single factual line containing {{APPROVED_VENDOR_ELIGIBILITY}} only when supplied. Set the action to {{APPROVED_APPLICATION_CTA}}, defaulting to “Apply to become a vendor” only when the linked destination is an application form. Add “Scan to view the opportunity” above the QR and {{VENDOR_APPLICATION_URL}} beneath it. Show no other claims.
Editable fields and name handling
Keep the university name, campus name, eligibility sentence, CTA, destination, photograph and QR as independent editable elements. Give the university module a maximum width of 760 px and permit two lines; use deliberate line breaks at natural word boundaries. Reduce its type size from 32 to no lower than 26 px before changing the layout. Never substitute an invented university, contact number, commission structure, onboarding date or minimum sales threshold. If eligibility is missing, remove that line and preserve the surrounding space.
QR and application component
Reserve a flat white 260 px square QR tile in the lower right, including a quiet zone of at least four modules on every side. Composite {{QR_ASSET}} exactly, without stylization, perspective, cropping, logo insertion or regenerated modules. Encode and verify {{VENDOR_APPLICATION_URL}}, never the general ordering page by default. Balance the tile with the invitation on the left. If the code or final route is missing, retain a blank editable slot in the production template and withhold the publication export.
Format adaptations
Reflow the story version to 1080 × 1920 px with essential content outside the top and bottom 250 px interface zones; move the photograph above the application strip and enlarge the scan area. Adapt the print version to A4 portrait with 3 mm bleed and at least 12 mm internal safety. Keep the QR at least 30 mm wide including its quiet zone, then validate it at print size. For a square version, reduce the photo height and remove optional eligibility copy before reducing essential text.
Specific exclusions
Exclude fictional revenue figures, guaranteed sales, instant onboarding, free partnership claims, invented fees, false campus logos, stock boardroom teams and technology-dashboard decoration. Do not use a student ordering CTA on a business recruitment design. Avoid imagery that suggests a vendor already belongs to Meal Direct without confirmation. Do not add celebratory award seals, fabricated app screenshots, sparkling food, fluorescent greens or unreadable kitchen overlays. Preserve the distinction between a vendor application and a confirmed partnership announcement.
Delivery and review
Deliver an editable master with clearly named brand, text, image, campus, CTA and QR layers, plus flat PNG exports and a print PDF where required. Name files MD_10_Vendor_Recruitment_{{CAMPUS_NAME}}_[format]. Review at full size and at 25% scale: the invitation must remain readable, the campus label must fit and the QR must retain an unobstructed boundary. Test the final exported QR on two devices and confirm that the resulting application destination matches the CTA before release.

prompts.title: Vendor Spotlight
prompts.body:
Objective and evidence
Create a Meal Direct spotlight for {{VENDOR_NAME}}, a verified participating vendor serving {{CAMPUS_NAME}} at {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}. Make the vendor and one authentic meal the focus, with a clear invitation to explore the approved offering. Confirm participation, image permission, product identity, availability and destination before publication. Treat a spotlight as an editorial introduction, not a review or award. If the vendor is unverified, retain this as an unpublished editable template; do not replace missing facts with a fictional food business.
Visual concept and layout
Build a 1080 × 1350 px portrait poster on 12 columns with 64 px safe margins. Use a large documentary photograph covering the right eight columns from the upper quarter to approximately 78% of the canvas. Place a deep-green vertical title field across the left five columns, allowing a controlled one-column overlap with the image. Put the vendor name in this field and a small Meal Direct attribution above it. Use a white lower utility band for campus details, destination and QR. Keep only one dominant photograph.
Identity and typographic hierarchy
Set the title field to #0B6B4F and the background to #F8FAFC or white. Use #074C39 for small structural rules, #BDE8D6 for one category label and #0F172A for body text. Set {{VENDOR_NAME}} in Outfit Bold at 76–102 px according to length, and secondary copy in Inter at 28–34 px. Place the exact approved {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} in an uncluttered upper or lower corner with at least half its symbol height of clear space. Never redraw or merge the Meal Direct and vendor marks. Place full /logofull.png on white at a size that preserves its embedded tagline; use approved /logo.png with separate Meal Direct text for narrow placements.
Authentic image direction
Use {{APPROVED_VENDOR_OR_MEAL_PHOTO}} as the product truth source. Preserve the actual dish composition, portion, packaging and ingredient appearance; do not generate a more expensive or fuller version of the food. If shooting new photography is possible, use a three-quarter close-up with soft window light, warm neutral surfaces and realistic steam only when appropriate to the dish. Retouch exposure, crop and background distractions gently. Never invent a vendor owner, storefront, staff portrait or customer scene. Leave the image slot blank when no authorized photo exists.
Complete visible copy
Use the small editorial label “VENDOR SPOTLIGHT”. Set the main title to “{{VENDOR_NAME}}” and the supporting line to “Meet a food vendor on Meal Direct.” Include {{VERIFIED_VENDOR_DESCRIPTOR}} only as a short factual description, such as an approved cuisine or specialty, without adding praise. Caption the photograph “{{FEATURED_MEAL_NAME}}”. Add {{APPROVED_AVAILABILITY_LINE}} only if current and campus-specific. Finish with “Explore this vendor”, “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}} • {{CAMPUS_NAME}}”, “Scan to view available meals” and {{VENDOR_DESTINATION_URL}}. Do not print the bullet if either campus field is absent.
Replaceable modules and length behavior
Keep vendor name, description, meal caption, availability, campus fields, photograph and destination independent. Allow the vendor name up to three deliberately balanced lines; do not crop letters or compress them horizontally. Allow the university name two lines in the lower information module, with a minimum 26 px size. Remove absent optional description or availability lines cleanly. If the approved destination shows more than this vendor, change the CTA to the accurate destination description and obtain the matching route before exporting.
Scan destination and QR treatment
Place a 260 px flat white QR tile on the lower right, including a minimum four-module quiet zone. Composite the supplied {{QR_ASSET}} intact and confirm that it opens {{VENDOR_DESTINATION_URL}} for the intended campus. Use a vendor-specific menu or listing when available; do not invent a route from the vendor name. Maintain at least 24 px separation from captions and branding. Keep a human-readable route beneath the tile. If assets are missing, use a blank editable slot without a simulated QR pattern.
Responsive and print versions
For a 1080 × 1920 px story, stack the vendor label, large vendor name, photo, short description and scan module in that order, protecting the top and bottom 250 px. For a square adaptation, show the photo on the right half and keep only the vendor name, meal caption, campus and CTA. For A4 print, use 3 mm bleed, 12 mm internal safety and a QR at least 30 mm wide including quiet zone. Preserve the authentic meal crop rather than stretching the image.
Specific negative direction
Exclude unverified “best”, “number one”, “student favourite”, star ratings, review counts, founding dates, certifications, discounts and stock scarcity. Do not substitute generic generated food while labeling it as the real vendor’s product. Avoid overlapping two logos into a new lockup, introducing the vendor’s palette as the dominant Meal Direct palette, or treating a business as an official university partner. Do not add map pins unless the approved location is known. Avoid multiple dish collages, noisy patterns and fake receipt fragments.
Export and verification
Deliver layered source files, a flat feed PNG, a story PNG and any requested print PDF. Name files MD_11_Vendor_Spotlight_{{VENDOR_NAME}}_{{CAMPUS_NAME}}_[format]. Attach an internal factual checklist identifying the supplied participation confirmation, photograph permission, featured dish and destination; keep that checklist outside the public artwork. Review vendor spelling, meal caption accuracy, image fidelity and campus-name wrapping. Scan the exported QR at final size and confirm current availability or remove the time-sensitive availability line before publication.

prompts.title: Menu Drop
prompts.body:
Objective and factual boundary
Create a menu announcement for {{VENDOR_NAME}} on Meal Direct at {{CAMPUS_NAME}}, {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}. Present an approved selection that students can inspect and act on without guessing prices or timing. Use only {{MENU_ITEMS_WITH_VERIFIED_PRICES}} and the supplied applicable dates, order window and scheduled delivery information. Confirm that every featured item is available through the destination at publication. If the source is a special menu, call it a special only when the vendor explicitly confirms that description.
Format and menu composition
Create a 1080 × 1350 px feed master on 12 columns with 64 px safety. Use a clean menu-sheet composition: a compact brand and campus masthead in the top 15%, a large title across the next 14%, three generously spaced menu rows across the next 45%, and a QR/order footer in the final 26%. Divide each row into item name, concise approved description and right-aligned price. Use thin rules and space rather than boxes around every item. Feature a maximum of three items per page.
Palette and typography
Use a predominantly white sheet with a #0B6B4F title and footer accent, #074C39 headings, #0F172A item names and #1E293B body text. Reserve #ECF7F2 for a subtle timing strip and #BDE8D6 for a single date label. Set “Menu drop” in Outfit Bold at approximately 94 px; use Outfit Semibold for item names at 40–46 px and Inter for descriptions and prices at 28–34 px. Align price numerals consistently. Composite {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} exactly, without redrawing or decorative recoloring. Place full /logofull.png on white at a size that preserves its embedded tagline; use approved /logo.png with separate Meal Direct text for narrow placements.
Food imagery and menu accuracy
Use one approved meal photo, positioned as a restrained crop beside the title or within one featured row, only if it shows the stated vendor’s actual product. Preserve portion size, toppings, packaging and plating. Prefer warm natural window light, gentle contrast and a clean neutral background. Do not generate food and present it as an authentic menu photograph. If no verified photo is supplied, produce a confident typography-only menu with greater negative space. Keep photography secondary to accurate menu content and readable prices.
Exact visible-copy system
Set the header to “MENU DROP”, the title to “{{VENDOR_NAME}}” and the campus line to “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}} / {{CAMPUS_NAME}}”. For each item, show its supplied name, approved short description and exact price with the supplied currency notation. Add “Available: {{APPROVED_MENU_DATE_OR_PERIOD}}” only when confirmed. Add “Order window: {{APPROVED_ORDER_WINDOW}}” and “Delivery window: {{APPROVED_DELIVERY_WINDOW}}” only when approved and applicable. Set the action to “View menu and order”, the scan label to “Scan for current availability” and the fallback to {{MENU_DESTINATION_URL}}.
Missing data and variable-length handling
Keep each menu item, description, price, timing field and image editable. Do not invent a third item to fill the layout. If only two items are supplied, increase row spacing. If more than three are supplied, create a numbered carousel or additional print page with the same header and verified destination. Let long item names wrap to two lines and remove optional descriptions before shrinking below 28 px. Allow the university field two lines. Omit unverified prices from publication and direct students to the current menu instead.
QR utility and operational clarity
Position the QR in a 250–280 px flat white tile at the lower right, with at least a four-module quiet zone. Use {{QR_ASSET}} as an exact composited asset pointing to {{MENU_DESTINATION_URL}}. Keep the QR away from menu rules and timing panels so its boundary remains clean. Include a short readable destination beneath it. Do not promise immediate delivery or imply that ordering is always open. Preserve a blank QR slot in editable drafts when the destination or asset is missing; never generate a decorative code.
Alternate formats
Reflow a story to 1080 × 1920 px with its essential content between the 250 px top and bottom protection zones; stack the three rows vertically and place the QR beside the final action. For menus with longer descriptions, use multiple story pages rather than tiny text. Adapt print to A4 with 3 mm bleed and 12 mm safe margins. Use a QR at least 30 mm wide including quiet zone. For counter-sized print, reduce the menu to one or two featured items and the scan action.
Exclusions and date discipline
Exclude fabricated crossed-out prices, invented savings, unverified vegetarian or allergen badges, artificial “sold out” markers, fake scarcity and sample menu items presented as available. Do not insert delivery fees, service fees, payment options or portion sizes unless supplied. Do not use an old menu photo to suggest current availability. Avoid long restaurant-style decorative scripts, patterned tablecloth backgrounds behind text and ingredient confetti. Make the validity period explicit when approved, and retire or update the artwork when that period ends.
Delivery and publication checks
Deliver the editable menu template with reusable row components, a feed PNG, any carousel continuation pages, story exports and a print-ready PDF when needed. Name files MD_12_Menu_Drop_{{VENDOR_NAME}}_{{CAMPUS_NAME}}_[date]_[format]. Compare every exported item, currency, amount and date character by character against the approved source. Test the QR on the final file and inspect the destination’s campus, vendor and menu. Review at thumbnail size and actual print size, confirming that the title, prices and ordering action remain distinct.

prompts.title: Vendor Benefits
prompts.body:
Objective and claim controls
Create a Meal Direct vendor-benefits explainer for food businesses considering service to {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}} and {{CAMPUS_NAME}}. Make the core message practical: understand how an approved campus partnership works and whether it fits the business. Base every benefit on {{APPROVED_VENDOR_BENEFITS}}, {{APPROVED_SCHEDULING_DESCRIPTION}} and {{APPROVED_VENDOR_WORKFLOW}}. Present campus discoverability and scheduled ordering only to the extent verified for the local service. Do not convert possible operational advantages into guaranteed sales, profit, growth, reduced waste or customer acquisition.
Distinct diagram composition
Use a 1080 × 1350 px canvas, an invisible 12-column grid and 64 px safety. Build a restrained three-stage diagram beneath a compact headline: a vendor meal offering on the left, a simple campus discovery panel in the center and an approved scheduling card on the right.
