Connect the stages with two meaningful, thin arrows. Give the diagram the middle 46% of the poster and reserve the lower quarter for the next step and QR. Use one continuous white background rather than a dashboard of unrelated boxes.
Color, type and exact logo
Use white and #ECF7F2 as the main field, #0B6B4F for the headline and arrows, #074C39 for diagram titles, #BDE8D6 for one highlighted scheduling card, and #0F172A for explanatory copy. Set the headline in Outfit Bold at 82–96 px, stage labels in Outfit Semibold at 36–42 px and descriptions in Inter at 28–32 px. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} at the upper left using the exact approved asset and its original proportions. Preserve clear space; do not invent a connected-network brand mark. Place full /logofull.png on white at a size that preserves its embedded tagline; use approved /logo.png with separate Meal Direct text for narrow placements.
Objects and illustration approach
Render the left stage as a realistic, unbranded packed meal photographed from above; treat it as illustrative food unless a verified vendor image is supplied. Represent campus discovery with a neutral editorial card containing approved words rather than a fabricated app interface. Represent scheduling with a typographic card containing {{APPROVED_SCHEDULING_DESCRIPTION}}, without invented dates or times. Use soft overhead light, tactile white paper edges and subtle contact shadows. Keep the visual metaphor legible and physically plausible. Do not add maps, dashboards or live data indicators.
Complete visible wording
Set the main headline to “See how Meal Direct fits your business.” Set the small campus module to “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}” and “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”. Use three approved labels selected from “Your food”, “Campus discovery” and “Scheduled orders” only when each accurately reflects the verified workflow. Place one short supplied benefit under each applicable stage, keeping the complete factual wording intact. End with “Explore vendor partnership”, “Scan for the details” and {{VENDOR_INFORMATION_URL}}. Do not invent percentage improvements, testimonials, operational guarantees or comparison claims.
Editable structure and evidence fallback
Keep each diagram stage, arrow, claim, campus label and destination independently editable. Attach source notes to the design file, outside the published artwork, for each benefit. If only two benefits are verified, use a two-stage composition with more space. If the workflow sequence is not confirmed, remove arrows and show the approved benefits as independent editorial columns. Allow the university name two lines at a minimum of 26 px. Never shrink a claim to unreadability to preserve the diagram; shorten only with approval.
QR and destination behavior
Use a 260 px flat white QR tile in the lower right, with a quiet zone of at least four modules. Composite {{QR_ASSET}} unchanged and verify that it opens {{VENDOR_INFORMATION_URL}}, a vendor information or partnership page. Use an application destination only if the CTA explicitly becomes “Apply to become a vendor”. Keep the human-readable route beside or beneath the tile. Do not point this business explainer to a student menu by default. Leave a blank editable module when an asset is missing.
Reflow and print adaptation
For the 1080 × 1920 px story, stack diagram stages vertically and change horizontal arrows to vertical connectors; protect the top and bottom 250 px. Keep each explanation close to its own stage. For a square feed format, retain two or three labels but move detailed descriptions into a second page when necessary. For A4 print, use 3 mm bleed, 12 mm safe margins and a QR at least 30 mm wide including quiet zone. Never shrink the full feed composition uniformly.
Specific exclusions
Exclude growth charts, cash piles, guaranteed orders, “zero risk”, “free”, “no fees”, “instant payouts”, invented commission terms and unsupported sales forecasts. Do not imply that Meal Direct handles packaging, provides equipment, owns a rider fleet or gives analytics unless those features are confirmed. Avoid abstract technology grids, glowing network lines, floating glossy phones and fabricated app screens. Do not use a university crest or the word “official” without authorization. Keep every annotation useful and every benefit connected to an actual approved service feature.
Delivery and review
Deliver an editable master with separate diagram objects, text, QR and campus modules, alongside feed and story PNGs and any required print PDF. Name files MD_13_Vendor_Benefits_{{CAMPUS_NAME}}_[format]. Review the flow with the person responsible for vendor operations to confirm that arrows, sequence and descriptions match reality. Inspect at 25% scale for a clear headline, readable stage labels and one obvious action. Verify contrast, long-name wrapping and final QR performance. Remove any unsupported benefit instead of filling empty space with generic marketing language.

prompts.title: Campus Ambassador
prompts.body:
Role objective and distinction
Create a Meal Direct campus ambassador recruitment poster for {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}, {{CAMPUS_NAME}}. Position this role around the approved brand outreach, content or campus activation responsibilities in {{APPROVED_AMBASSADOR_ROLE_SUMMARY}}. Keep it distinct from a student representative role focused on peer referrals and community assistance. Publish only when a real vacancy, eligibility criteria, responsibilities, application route and role terms are confirmed. Do not imply employment, paid compensation, free meals, certificates, academic credit or exclusive university endorsement unless explicitly approved.
Primary format and composition
Create a 1080 × 1350 px portrait master with 12 columns, 64 px safe margins and deliberate asymmetry. Use a candid student photograph in a large vertical panel across the left seven columns, occupying about 62% of the height. Place an oversized three-line headline across the right seven columns, overlapping only an uncluttered part of the photo. Keep the lower third as a clean recruitment panel containing role essentials, campus and application. Make the role title immediately visible before the person’s face or supporting details.
Brand and typography treatment
Use a #0B6B4F brand field with white headline text, #ECF7F2 for the lower information panel, #074C39 for role details and #BDE8D6 for one small recruitment label. Set the main title in Outfit Bold at 92–110 px with tight but legible spacing. Use Inter at 28–32 px for responsibilities and 24–28 px for eligibility and deadline. Composite the exact {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} on a plain area that supports its official colors. Preserve the asset’s proportions and clear space rather than creating a special ambassador logo. Place full /logofull.png on white at a size that preserves its embedded tagline; use approved /logo.png with separate Meal Direct text for narrow placements.
Human image direction
Use {{APPROVED_STUDENT_PHOTO}} with appropriate permission, showing a natural campus moment such as preparing event materials, discussing a simple creative idea or recording approved content. Capture realistic gestures, comfortable everyday clothing and ordinary campus surroundings in soft daylight. Do not portray the person as a current ambassador unless that status is confirmed. If a real image is unavailable, use an openly illustrative crop of a notebook, phone and unbranded tote without a face, university insignia or fabricated campaign materials. Avoid artificial team poses.
Complete proposed copy
Set the headline as “Be a campus / ambassador.” with the line break adjusted only for balance. Use the supporting line “Help introduce Meal Direct on your campus.” Place “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}” and “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}” in the campus module. Include {{APPROVED_AMBASSADOR_ROLE_SUMMARY}} and up to three concise {{APPROVED_AMBASSADOR_RESPONSIBILITIES}}. Add “Who can apply: {{APPROVED_ELIGIBILITY}}” and “Apply by: {{APPROVED_APPLICATION_DEADLINE}}” only when supplied. Set the CTA to “Apply for the ambassador role”, the scan label to “Scan for role details” and the route to {{AMBASSADOR_APPLICATION_URL}}.
Verified terms and flexible modules
Keep the photo, university, campus, responsibilities, eligibility, deadline and role terms fully editable. Let long university names span two lines; preserve full spelling and a minimum 26 px size. Keep role terms on the destination page when they are too long for the poster, without hiding material obligations. Remove the deadline block if recruitment is ongoing and no closing date is confirmed. Do not add invented requirements such as follower counts, age thresholds, faculty restrictions or previous experience. Leave absent facts out rather than completing them speculatively.
QR and application panel
Reserve a flat white 260 px QR tile in the lower right, including at least a four-module quiet zone. Composite {{QR_ASSET}} exactly and test that it opens {{AMBASSADOR_APPLICATION_URL}} for the specified campus and role. Use a direct application or role-details route; do not substitute a referral registration link. Keep the CTA to the left and the readable URL beneath. If the QR asset or route is missing, provide a blank editable production slot and withhold the public-ready export until it can be completed.
Format reflow
For a 1080 × 1920 px story, place the headline above the image, the approved responsibilities below it and the application module above the bottom 250 px protection zone; reserve 250 px at the top as well. For A4 noticeboard print, use 3 mm bleed and 12 mm safe margins, with the title visible from a distance and the QR at least 30 mm wide including quiet zone. For a square post, omit optional detail and direct viewers to the full role description.
Negative direction
Exclude fake testimonials from ambassadors, invented income figures, “earn big”, guaranteed selection, misleading job language, free-product promises and forced youth slang. Do not use a campus crest, graduation gown, institutional seal or “official university ambassador” unless authorized. Avoid influencer follower counters, artificial crowd scenes, floating social-media logos and fake chat screenshots. Keep the student representative concept out of this artwork unless the supplied role explicitly includes it. Do not crowd the poster with every possible responsibility or make the QR compete with a decorative sticker.
Delivery and review
Deliver separate editable text, photograph, campus, role-detail and QR layers plus flat feed and story PNGs and the requested print PDF. Name files MD_14_Campus_Ambassador_{{CAMPUS_NAME}}_[format]. Review role wording against the approved brief, confirm photo permission and ensure no benefit was added by implication. Test the final QR on two devices, check the application identifies the correct campus and role, and review the poster at 25% scale. Keep the headline, role distinction and action clear before approving publication.

prompts.title: Student Representative
prompts.body:
Recruitment purpose and role distinction
Create a Meal Direct student representative recruitment design for {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}, {{CAMPUS_NAME}}. Present the approved role as a practical connection between Meal Direct and the campus community, using {{APPROVED_REPRESENTATIVE_ROLE_SUMMARY}}. Distinguish it from the campus ambassador campaign: emphasize approved peer referrals, community questions and link sharing rather than automatically assigning content production, public appearances or event leadership. Confirm that this exact role exists before publication. Describe compensation, obligations and eligibility only from approved terms; do not invent commissions, salaries, targets or benefits.
Editorial concept and composition
Build a 1080 × 1350 px feed master on 12 columns with 64 px safe margins. Use a paper-based editorial composition: a large headline across the top 32%, three simple connected information strips through the middle 34%, and a recruitment action panel in the lower 34%. Make the information strips resemble orderly community notes, not fabricated social-media messages. Connect them with one restrained directional line to suggest useful information being shared. Use asymmetric placement and ample white space while keeping every strip aligned to the underlying grid.
Brand and type system
Use #ECF7F2 as the background, #0B6B4F for the headline and connector, white for paper strips, #074C39 for their labels and #0F172A for details. Use #BDE8D6 only for a small campus marker. Set the headline in Outfit Bold at 88–104 px, strip labels in Outfit Semibold at 36–42 px and supporting text in Inter at 28–32 px. Place the exact approved full {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} on a sufficiently large white panel, or use the approved icon with separate Meal Direct text for a narrow placement. Never redraw or recolor the asset.
Objects, texture and depth
Use tactile paper notes, a plain pencil and a subtle notebook edge as supporting objects. Keep the objects unbranded and secondary to the message. Photograph or render them from a nearly overhead viewpoint with broad soft daylight from the upper left, believable contact shadows and a restrained off-white paper texture. Keep the three note strips visually consistent and avoid excessive tape, stickers or torn edges. Do not add screenshots, profile photographs, message counts or names that could be mistaken for actual student conversations or testimonials.
Complete proposed visible copy
Set the headline to “Help your campus / find Meal Direct.” Use the role label “STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES”. Add “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}” and “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}” as separate editable campus lines. Populate up to three note strips with concise {{APPROVED_REPRESENTATIVE_RESPONSIBILITIES}}; use “Share the campus link”, “Help with questions” and “Support your community” only if those duties are confirmed. Add {{APPROVED_REPRESENTATIVE_ROLE_SUMMARY}} beneath the headline. Set the CTA to “Apply as a student representative”, the QR caption to “Scan for the role details” and the route to {{REPRESENTATIVE_APPLICATION_URL}}.
Terms and replacement behavior
Add “Who can apply: {{APPROVED_ELIGIBILITY}}” and “Apply by: {{APPROVED_APPLICATION_DEADLINE}}” only when those inputs are supplied and current. Keep {{APPROVED_ROLE_TERMS}} accessible at the linked destination; summarize material commitments accurately if the approved brief requires them on the poster. Allow a two-line university name without abbreviation, with a minimum 26 px size. Reduce the number of responsibility strips when fewer are verified. Never fill empty space with invented duties, earnings, experience requirements, application deadlines or a suggestion that the university has endorsed the program.
Application QR component
Reserve a 260 px square white tile in the lower right, including a quiet zone of at least four modules. Composite {{QR_ASSET}} intact and verify that it opens {{REPRESENTATIVE_APPLICATION_URL}} for this role and campus. Use an actual application or role-details page, not the student food-ordering route or an unverified referral link. Keep the action beside the tile and a readable fallback URL below it. Leave a blank editable QR slot when the verified asset is missing; do not generate a simulated code.
Adaptation instructions
For a 1080 × 1920 px story, stack the role label, headline, note strips and application panel vertically while keeping essential content outside the top and bottom 250 px. Retain only the two most important responsibilities if space becomes tight. For A4 recruitment print, use 3 mm bleed and 12 mm internal safety; keep the QR at least 30 mm wide including its quiet zone. For a square post, keep one strong responsibility plus the headline, campus and CTA. Rebuild the arrangement instead of uniformly shrinking it.
Specific negative direction
Exclude fabricated group chats, fake student names, invented testimonials, follower counters, recruitment badges, income claims and guaranteed acceptance. Do not describe the role as an internship or employment unless verified. Avoid promising free meals, certificates, exclusive access, referral cash or unlimited rewards. Keep ambassador wording out of the role label. Do not make the directional line look like a multilevel marketing structure, and do not show chains of money or recruitment tiers. Keep the design useful, inclusive and focused on the actual approved responsibilities.
Deliverables and checks
Deliver an editable master with separate note-strip, typography, logo, campus and QR components, plus feed and story PNGs and any requested print PDF. Name files MD_15_Student_Representative_{{CAMPUS_NAME}}_[format]. Review every responsibility and term against the approved role description. Inspect long university names, body-copy contrast and visual hierarchy at 25% scale. Test the exported QR on two devices and confirm that the correct representative application opens. Remove unsupported details rather than adding generic recruitment promises to make the design feel fuller.

prompts.title: Delivery Partner
prompts.body:
Objective and local operating facts
Create a Meal Direct delivery-partner recruitment design for {{CAMPUS_NAME}} at {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}. Invite eligible applicants to review {{APPROVED_DELIVERY_ROLE_TITLE}} and apply through the verified destination. Use only the approved transport types, responsibilities, eligibility requirements and role terms. Confirm whether this campus uses riders, runners or another defined model before choosing imagery or wording. Do not imply employment status, flexible hours, guaranteed earnings, provided equipment, insurance or vehicle ownership requirements unless those details are explicitly confirmed for this opportunity.
Layout and focal hierarchy
Build a 1080 × 1350 px portrait master on 12 columns with 64 px safe margins. Use a strong diagonal photographic crop across the middle 48% of the page, created by the subject’s natural movement rather than a decorative brand slash. Position a large headline in a white upper field and a deep-green application panel below. Keep the delivery bag or approved transport detail as the visual focal point, then the role title, then the application. Preserve a clean lower-right QR zone without perspective or motion effects.
Palette, logo and typography
Use white for the upper field, #0B6B4F for the application panel, #074C39 for a single structural label, #BDE8D6 for a small eligibility marker and #0F172A for dark text. Set the main headline in Outfit Bold at 90–108 px and supporting details in Inter at 28–34 px. Use only the exact approved {{LOGO_PRIMARY}}; retain the full logo on a white panel at a size where its embedded tagline is legible. For a narrow placement, use the approved icon with separate Meal Direct text, without inventing a lockup.
Photography and practical realism
Use {{APPROVED_DELIVERY_PHOTO}} when available, showing an authorized person and the locally permitted transport or walking delivery context. Prefer a candid side view on a realistic campus path, a securely closed food bag, natural daylight and a credible posture. Show safety equipment and road behavior consistent with the approved local policy. If no real photo is available, use a clearly illustrative close crop of a plain insulated bag without people, badges or a vehicle. Do not add unauthorized branding or imply that the pictured equipment is supplied by Meal Direct.
Complete visible-copy plan
Set the headline to “Help deliver meals / across campus.” Use the role label “{{APPROVED_DELIVERY_ROLE_TITLE}}” and the location lines “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}” and “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”. Include one concise line from {{APPROVED_DELIVERY_RESPONSIBILITIES}}. Add “Who can apply: {{APPROVED_ELIGIBILITY_AND_SAFETY_REQUIREMENTS}}” only when the approved text can fit legibly; otherwise use “View eligibility and role details”. Set the primary action to “Apply to be a delivery partner”, the QR caption to “Scan for the opportunity” and the fallback route to {{DELIVERY_PARTNER_APPLICATION_URL}}. Add no earnings claim.
Flexible terms and transport handling
Make role title, transport image, eligibility, responsibilities, campus and destination independent editable modules. Use “rider” or “runner” only when the verified role actually requires that mode. Allow the university name two lines and preserve its full official spelling; reduce its size only to 26 px before widening its module. Keep material role terms accurately stated at the destination and surface any required limitation in the approved poster copy. Remove absent schedules or application deadlines instead of creating them. Do not infer eligibility from a person’s appearance.
Functional QR and link
Place {{QR_ASSET}} inside a 260 px square flat white tile, including at least a four-module quiet zone. Composite the supplied code without regenerating modules, cropping its edges, adding logos or applying a green tint. Confirm that it opens {{DELIVERY_PARTNER_APPLICATION_URL}} for the correct campus opportunity. Keep the tile separated from the photograph and its implied movement. Add the readable URL beneath it. If no final application route or code exists, retain a blank editable slot and mark the working file as incomplete outside the public artwork.
Story and print reflow
For the 1080 × 1920 px story, place the headline and role label first, the cropped photograph second, and the application module third, protecting the top and bottom 250 px. Keep any required eligibility text above the CTA. For an A4 campus recruitment poster, add 3 mm bleed, preserve 12 mm internal safety and use a QR at least 30 mm wide including quiet zone. For a square version, reduce the photo height and keep only essential role information. Do not shrink legal or eligibility copy to decorative size.
Specific exclusions
Exclude speed streaks, reckless riding, unfastened helmets where required, unrealistic stacks of food, unsecured bags, money rain and unsupported daily earnings. Do not show motorcycles, bicycles, cars or pedestrians interchangeably without confirming the operating model. Avoid “start today”, “work whenever”, “guaranteed income”, “no experience needed” and “equipment provided” unless approved. Do not invent delivery distances, working windows, rider tracking, payout schedules or customer ratings. Keep the poster an honest opportunity announcement rather than a promise of employment or a claim of instant meal delivery.
Delivery and approval checks
Deliver editable layers for the image, role title, eligibility, campus, CTA and QR, plus flat feed and story PNGs and the requested print PDF. Name files MD_16_Delivery_Partner_{{CAMPUS_NAME}}_[format]. Verify the image against local transport and safety requirements and compare all wording with the approved role brief. Inspect at 25% scale for a clear recruitment message and readable location. Scan the final QR on two devices, confirm that the correct application opens, and check that the linked terms match the artwork before publication.

prompts.title: How to Order
prompts.body:
Learning objective and verified flow
Create a Meal Direct instructional design that helps a new student understand the macro sequence “Scan, choose, order, eat” for {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}, {{CAMPUS_NAME}}. Make the first action unmistakable while preserving the real checkout requirements in {{APPROVED_ORDERING_STEPS}} and {{APPROVED_CHECKOUT_DETAILS}}. Confirm the campus route, selection process, payment description and scheduled delivery behavior before publication. Treat the four words as a clear summary, not a claim that ordering contains only four taps or that food arrives immediately after payment.
Canvas and stepped composition
Create a 1080 × 1350 px portrait master using 12 columns and 64 px safe margins. Place the headline in the top 20%, then arrange four numbered steps as a descending staircase through the central 57%, with the final scan action in the lower 23%. Let each step shift one column to the right while keeping labels and descriptions aligned within each block. Use a single thin connector to show sequence. Keep the QR separate from illustrative icons so viewers identify the functional code immediately.
Identity and typographic rhythm
Use white as the main field, #0B6B4F for the headline and step numbers, #074C39 for step labels, #ECF7F2 for alternating background bands and #BDE8D6 for one final-step accent. Use #0F172A for descriptions. Set the headline in Outfit Bold at 84–98 px, step labels in Outfit Semibold at 44–50 px and descriptions in Inter at 28–32 px. Place the approved {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} on a white panel, without cropping its embedded tagline. Use the approved icon and separate Meal Direct text if the available slot is narrow.
Icons and product evidence
Use four simple editorial symbols: a small scan-frame outline, a meal-selection card, an order checklist and a plated meal. Keep icon strokes consistent and avoid decorative detail. The scan symbol must contain no QR-like random pattern. If {{APPROVED_PRODUCT_SCREENSHOTS}} are supplied, use one accurate crop to support the relevant step without changing interface labels or inventing buttons. Otherwise use abstract, clearly noninteractive cards containing only approved text. Apply soft paper shadows and minimal texture; keep the sequence flat and readable rather than building a glossy phone mockup.
Exact proposed visible copy
Set the headline to “Your next meal, / step by step.” Set the four labels exactly to “01 Scan”, “02 Choose”, “03 Order” and “04 Eat”. Use “Open your campus link.” for Scan and “Choose from available meals.” for Choose. Populate Order with {{APPROVED_CHECKOUT_DETAILS}}, including the verified delivery-window, location and payment requirements. Populate Eat with {{APPROVED_DELIVERY_WINDOW_DESCRIPTION}} rather than an instant-arrival promise. Add “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}”, “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”, “Start with your campus link”, “Scan to explore meals” and {{CAMPUS_URL}}. Show no extra process claims.
Checkout clarity and flexible text
Keep every description editable and accurate to the real ordering flow. If the approved campus flow includes selecting an available delivery window, entering delivery details and paying upfront, include those actions in the Order description in the correct sequence. Do not add account creation, cash on delivery, live tracking, saved addresses, pickup or cancellation options without confirmation. Allow the campus name module two lines at a minimum 26 px. If the Order description is too long, expand that step vertically or add a supporting slide instead of omitting a required action.
QR execution and fallback
Place the genuine {{QR_ASSET}} in a 260 px square flat white tile with a minimum four-module quiet zone. Keep the code at the lower right, aligned with the start-action text, and verify that it opens {{CAMPUS_URL}} for the intended university and campus. Never generate the code as part of an image or duplicate it inside an illustrative phone. Include the readable campus URL below. If the final route or asset is unavailable, leave a blank editable slot and withhold the final publication export.
Adaptation strategy
For a 1080 × 1920 px story, change the staircase into a vertical sequence with four full-width rows, protecting the top and bottom 250 px. Keep the actual QR in the final utility row. For a carousel, use an overview page followed by detailed steps, retaining numbering and a scan destination on the final page. For A4 print, use 3 mm bleed, 12 mm safe margins and a QR at least 30 mm wide including quiet zone. Keep the order requirements readable at final print size.
Specific negative direction
Exclude countdown timers, lightning-bolt speed claims, “instant delivery”, “one tap”, “no signup” and “pay on delivery” unless the exact feature is verified. Do not present decorative screens as actual Meal Direct product screenshots. Avoid multiple competing arrows, tiny text inside phones, complex isometric journeys and food imagery that overwhelms instructions. Do not skip scheduled delivery or payment requirements to make the process seem shorter. Keep “Eat” as the final outcome, with fulfillment described accurately rather than implying the meal appears immediately after ordering.
Delivery and flow review
Deliver an editable process template with separate numbered steps, text, icons, logo, campus and QR modules, plus feed and story PNGs and requested print or carousel files. Name files MD_17_How_to_Order_{{CAMPUS_NAME}}_[format]. Walk through the live approved campus ordering flow and compare each step with the artwork. Check sequence, payment wording, delivery-window language and any screenshot accuracy. Test the exported QR, review the diagram at 25% scale and verify that a new student can identify both the first action and the required checkout details.

prompts.title: How It Works
prompts.body:
Objective and information standard
Create a Meal Direct explainer that answers the practical questions a new student has before ordering at {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}, {{CAMPUS_NAME}}: how payment works, when meals are delivered and how fulfillment happens. Use {{APPROVED_PAYMENT_DESCRIPTION}}, {{APPROVED_DELIVERY_WINDOW_DESCRIPTION}} and {{APPROVED_FULFILLMENT_DESCRIPTION}} as mandatory factual inputs. Verify campus-specific implementation even when a general website describes upfront payment and selected delivery windows. Do not fill unknown details with industry assumptions. Keep the design unpublished if a core answer is missing or contradicts the current service.
Composition and distinct visual structure
Build a 1080 × 1350 px master on a 12-column grid with 64 px safe margins. Use an editorial answer-sheet layout, distinct from the four-step ordering poster. Place a confident title in the top 22%, then use three broad horizontal information bands labeled Payment, Timing and Delivery across the next 51%. Reserve the lower 27% for the campus label, a concise next action and QR. Keep the bands open and spacious, separated by thin rules rather than rounded dashboard cards. Make practical answers the focal point.
Palette, identity and hierarchy
Use #0B6B4F as a narrow vertical side rail and for the headline, white for the main reading field, #ECF7F2 for one timing emphasis and #074C39 for category labels. Set descriptive text in #0F172A and secondary notes in #1E293B. Use Outfit Bold at 88–102 px for the title, Outfit Semibold at 36–42 px for the category labels and Inter at 30–34 px for explanations. Composite the exact {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} on a white panel large enough for the full asset, or use the approved compact icon treatment.
Supporting visual language
Use three small, restrained line symbols: a payment confirmation symbol, a calendar-window symbol and a meal-handover symbol. Keep them secondary to the written explanations and avoid depicting unsupported payment brands or delivery equipment. Use flat editorial drawing with consistent strokes and no simulated interface controls. Add an understated paper texture only outside text and scan areas. If an approved real fulfillment photograph is supplied, use a narrow crop as a footer accent without changing the three-answer hierarchy. Do not create a fake receipt or tracking screen.
Complete visible-copy framework
Set the headline to “Know how / your order works.” Set the category labels exactly to “Payment”, “Timing” and “Delivery”. Under Payment, insert {{APPROVED_PAYMENT_DESCRIPTION}}. Under Timing, insert {{APPROVED_DELIVERY_WINDOW_DESCRIPTION}} and, only when needed, {{APPROVED_ORDER_CUTOFF_DESCRIPTION}}. Under Delivery, insert {{APPROVED_FULFILLMENT_DESCRIPTION}}. Add the campus lines “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}” and “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”. Set the action to “Explore your campus menu”, the QR caption to “Scan to get started” and the route to {{CAMPUS_URL}}. Add “Need help? {{APPROVED_SUPPORT_ROUTE}}” only when that route is confirmed and monitored.
Accuracy and content-length rules
Explain scheduled delivery using the approved selection and fulfillment wording; do not turn a selectable window into a precise arrival guarantee. State upfront payment only when confirmed for the target campus and explain accepted methods only from verified input. Clarify pickup versus delivery, approved handover location, recipient responsibility or order cutoff only when those facts apply. Keep each answer to a readable short paragraph; create an additional page if essential details exceed the layout. Allow the university name two lines without abbreviation and retain a minimum 26 px size.
QR, route and publication readiness
Reserve a 260 px flat white QR tile in the lower right, with an untouched quiet zone of at least four modules. Composite {{QR_ASSET}} exactly and confirm that it opens {{CAMPUS_URL}}. Keep the campus ordering route as the primary action, and give any support route a clearly secondary text treatment. Never encode an unapproved shortened address or use a decorative generated QR pattern. Retain a blank editable scan slot when the final asset is unavailable. Do not publish until the operational facts and the destination are both verified.
Adaptations for different contexts
For a 1080 × 1920 px story, stack the three answers with generous vertical separation inside the top and bottom 250 px protection zones, followed by the scan action. For a carousel, dedicate one page to each operational topic and put the campus link on the final page. For A4 print, use 3 mm bleed, 12 mm safe margins and a QR at least 30 mm wide including quiet zone. For compact formats, keep only approved short answers and move detail to the verified destination.
Specific exclusions and clarity checks
Exclude unsupported refund rules, cancellation rights, tracking features, delivery-fee claims, guaranteed arrival times, payment logos, cash-on-delivery promises and customer-service response times. Do not imply 24-hour operations, immediate dispatch or doorstep delivery when those are not confirmed. Avoid generic fintech imagery, padlock badges, fake payment success screens and invented order numbers. Keep explanations factual and plain; do not use legalistic text to conceal uncertainty. Remove any statement that cannot be matched to the approved campus operations brief before presenting the design as publication-ready.
Deliverables and final validation
Deliver an editable master with independent Payment, Timing, Delivery, campus, support and QR modules, plus feed and story PNGs and any requested print or carousel files. Name files MD_18_How_It_Works_{{CAMPUS_NAME}}_[format]. Have the responsible operations reviewer compare each public statement with current campus practice. Test the final exported QR and support route, confirm contrast and long-name wrapping, and review at 25% scale. Check that the design answers practical questions without implying any additional service feature through icons, labels or imagery.

prompts.title: Student Voice
prompts.body:
Select the truthful campaign mode
Create a Meal Direct student-voice design for {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}, {{CAMPUS_NAME}}. Choose Quote mode only when {{VERIFIED_STUDENT_QUOTE}}, {{APPROVED_STUDENT_ATTRIBUTION}} and {{QUOTE_AND_IMAGE_PERMISSION}} are supplied and verified. Use Feedback mode when those conditions are not met. In Quote mode, present the student’s actual words without inventing praise or changing the meaning. In Feedback mode, invite a response without suggesting that positive feedback already exists. Do not turn an AI-generated person, composite statement or sample quote into apparent customer evidence.
Editorial composition
Build a 1080 × 1350 px portrait master using 12 columns and 64 px safe margins. In Quote mode, give the authorized quotation the upper 48% of the canvas and place a small real portrait or approved contextual photograph across the middle-right area; keep attribution close to the quote. In Feedback mode, replace the quotation field with a large question and use an unbranded notebook or meal-packaging detail as the supporting image. Reserve the lower 27% for campus, one CTA and the QR. Keep whitespace generous.
Palette, logo and typographic voice
Use #ECF7F2 as the reading background, #0B6B4F for the quotation or question, #074C39 for attribution, #0F172A for support copy and white for the scan panel. Use #BDE8D6 only for a small editorial label. Set the main text in Outfit Semibold at 64–82 px, with line breaks that preserve natural reading. Use Inter at 28–32 px for attribution and secondary copy. Composite the exact {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} on white at a legible size; use the approved icon and separate Meal Direct text only when space requires a compact treatment.
Authentic photography and permission
Use {{APPROVED_STUDENT_PHOTO}} only within the scope of the student’s explicit permission and approved attribution. Preserve the person’s identity and appearance; do not beautify, replace or generate their face. Prefer natural window light, ordinary campus surroundings and relaxed documentary framing. Do not imply that a stock model is the reviewer. If photo permission is absent, use a typography-led quote layout without a portrait. In Feedback mode, use a neutral overhead still life of a notebook and unbranded food container, with soft shadows and no fabricated handwritten testimonial.
Complete Quote-mode copy
Set the editorial label to “STUDENT VOICE”. Insert “{{VERIFIED_STUDENT_QUOTE}}” exactly, with appropriate quotation marks and only approved punctuation changes. Place {{APPROVED_STUDENT_ATTRIBUTION}} immediately below, using only the name, initial, course or campus detail that the student authorized. Add “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}” and “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}” in the location module. Use “Explore Meal Direct on your campus”, “Scan to view available meals” and {{CAMPUS_URL}} for the action. Do not add star ratings, satisfaction scores, purchase counts or claims that this opinion represents all students.
Complete Feedback-mode copy and flexibility
Set the editorial label to “STUDENT VOICE” and the main question to {{APPROVED_FEEDBACK_QUESTION}}, defaulting to “Tried Meal Direct? / Tell us what you think.” Use “Your feedback helps us understand your experience.” as supporting copy only when the response process genuinely accepts feedback. Set the action to “Share your feedback”, the QR caption to “Scan to leave a response” and the route to {{FEEDBACK_DESTINATION_URL}}. Keep feedback neutral, without requiring praise. Allow the university name two lines and shorten no quotation without explicit approval.
Mode-specific QR and missing inputs
Use a 260 px square flat white QR tile with a minimum four-module quiet zone. Composite {{QR_ASSET}} intact and verify the destination selected by the campaign mode: {{CAMPUS_URL}} for exploring the service after a genuine quote, or {{FEEDBACK_DESTINATION_URL}} for submitting feedback. Never use a student-ordering code beneath a feedback CTA. Leave the QR slot blank in working templates when the destination is unconfirmed. If no review permission exists, switch the whole composition to Feedback mode rather than retaining quotation marks, attribution or a suggestive portrait.
Format adaptation
For a 1080 × 1920 px story, keep the quote or question in the upper central area, the image or attribution beneath it and the action above the bottom 250 px protection zone; protect the top 250 px as well. If an authorized quotation is too long, create a carousel using approved complete excerpts rather than shrinking it. For A4 print, use 3 mm bleed, 12 mm safe margins and a QR at least 30 mm wide including quiet zone. Preserve readable attribution and the mode-specific CTA.
Specific negative direction
Exclude fictional student names, invented reviews, generated customer portraits, altered sentiment, unapproved university affiliations and star-rating graphics without evidence. Do not imply that a quotation proves typical results, guaranteed satisfaction or university endorsement. Avoid speech bubbles resembling real chat screenshots, fabricated timestamps, app-review badges and anonymous claims presented as verified purchases. Do not offer prizes, discounts or free meals for feedback unless an actual approved campaign supplies those terms. Keep the feedback question open and respectful, without steering users toward a predetermined positive answer.
Delivery and authenticity checks
Deliver an editable Quote-mode or Feedback-mode master, clearly named outside the artwork, with separate quote/question, attribution, image, campus, CTA and QR components. Export flat feed and story PNGs and any required print PDF. Name files MD_19_Student_Voice_{{MODE_QUOTE_OR_FEEDBACK}}_{{CAMPUS_NAME}}_[format]. Compare quote wording and attribution against the permission record, verify image usage and test the final QR. Review at 25% scale for clear hierarchy. Confirm that the published design cannot be mistaken for a genuine review when it is only requesting feedback.

prompts.title: Weekly Pick
prompts.body:
01 — Communication job and verification
Create a premium editorial Weekly Pick that makes one actual meal immediately desirable and sends students to the relevant campus menu. The first read is the meal, the second is its vendor, and the third is the discovery action. Use only a confirmed participating vendor and a real available meal, with the supplied week label. Treat the selection as an editorial feature, never as a bestseller, student favorite, award winner, discounted special, or nutrition claim unless separately substantiated. Omit an unverified price entirely.
02 — Format and composition map
Build the primary artwork at 1080 × 1350 pixels with 64-pixel outer safety margins and an invisible 12-column grid. Use a dark-green canvas. Reserve the top 13% for the logo, campus label, and a compact week marker. Let a single food photograph occupy approximately the central 53%, with the dish extending slightly into the neighboring text zone. Place the display headline in the upper-left negative space, the meal and vendor attribution below the hero, and a mint information rail along the bottom. Keep this asymmetrical but precisely aligned.
03 — Typography and complete copy
Use Outfit ExtraBold at approximately 100–116 pixels for “This week’s pick.”, with a deliberate break after “week’s” if needed. Set {{MEAL_NAME}} at 52–64 pixels, {{VENDOR_NAME}} at 30–36 pixels, and functional labels in Inter at 26–30 pixels. Include only this proposed copy: “WEEKLY PICK”; “{{WEEK_LABEL}}”; “This week’s pick.”; “{{MEAL_NAME}}”; “From {{VENDOR_NAME}}”; “Explore this pick on your campus menu.”; “Scan to explore”; and the supplied university, campus, and route. Add a verified price only as a quiet factual line, never a promotional burst.
04 — Identity, palette, and logo
Use primary green #0B6B4F, dark green #074C39, mint #BDE8D6, pale green #ECF7F2, white, and optional slate #0F172A/#1E293B/#F8FAFC. Use Outfit display type and Inter functional text. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} intact from Meal Direct’s /logofull.png or /logo.png; preserve proportions, colors, and padding. Never redraw, recolor, crop, or recreate its tagline. Transfer the reference’s editorial restraint, never its purple identity or symbols. Use dark green for the canvas, mint for the lower rail, and white for the scan reserve.
05 — Food image and tactile treatment
Use {{VERIFIED_MEAL_PHOTO}} of the actual featured product, or a vendor-approved photo that accurately represents the serving. Prefer a three-quarter overhead angle, natural side light from the upper left, visible grain and texture, believable portions, and a clean ceramic or takeaway presentation appropriate to that meal. Retain truthful ingredient colors. Separate the plate from the background with a soft physical shadow. Do not invent garnishes, extra proteins, side dishes, packaging, or portion sizes. A very subtle background-paper texture may add depth; protect food detail, type, and all utility components.
06 — University and variable modules
Keep university, campus, headline, copy, URL, logo, and QR separately editable. Reserve two lines for {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}; expand the module before shrinking text. Never condense, truncate, or invent abbreviations. Omit a duplicate campus label. Realign neighboring modules after replacement. No university crest or implied institutional endorsement without approval. Let an unusually long meal name occupy up to three lines within its designated caption area; reduce the photograph’s height slightly instead of making the meal name unreadable.
07 — QR and destination behavior
Place {{QR_ASSET}} in a flat pure-white square in the bottom-right rail, beginning at approximately 210 pixels outer width for the feed layout, then verify against its actual density. Preserve the entire genuine code and a clear quiet zone of at least four modules on every side. Keep “Scan to explore” outside that quiet zone. Display {{CAMPUS_URL}} as the human-readable fallback beside the code. Verify that the destination reveals the relevant campus and current selection. Never generate a decorative QR pattern, fake application screen, fabricated menu listing, or unsupported direct-to-cart behavior.
08 — Controlled supporting detail
Use one thin editorial rule or one modest arrow to connect the food caption with the discovery rail. If {{AVAILABILITY_NOTE}} is supplied, include it in small but legible text above the CTA, using the exact approved wording. Do not fill empty space with stars, ratings, order counts, trending stickers, fake scarcity, or overlapping badges. Keep the image responsible for appetite and the text responsible for factual identity. Ensure mint labels remain dark-green on mint rather than mint on white.
09 — Reflow and output adaptations
For 1080 × 1920 stories, stack the headline, taller hero crop, factual caption, and QR rail; maintain 64-pixel side margins and keep essential content clear of platform interface areas. Add a separate link-sticker placement area without pretending a printed link is tappable. For A4 print, recompose on 210 × 297 millimeters with 3-millimeter bleed and 10-millimeter safety, use 300-ppi effective photography, and start with a 35–40-millimeter outer QR. Export print PDF/X-4 using the printer-confirmed ICC profile; do not apply an arbitrary CMYK conversion.
10 — Final delivery and checks
Deliver named editable layers, linked photographs, live text, intact logos, and replaceable QR, plus flat exports. Verify spelling, facts, rights, destination, and week-specific availability. Inspect at 25% and 100%. Remove useless decoration. Mark incomplete versions as review proofs; do not publish unresolved tokens.

prompts.title: Noticeboard
prompts.body:
01 — Communication job and truth conditions
Create a printed noticeboard poster that introduces Meal Direct to students passing between classes. It must communicate a useful ordering destination in one glance and provide a straightforward scan when someone steps closer. Publish an ordering invitation only when the named campus route is active. If launch status is unknown, keep the artwork as a review proof until confirmed. Describe Meal Direct accurately as scheduled campus meal delivery; never imply immediate dispatch, universal vendor coverage, guaranteed delivery times, or official university sponsorship.
02 — Print format and structural grid
Design the master at A3 portrait, 297 × 420 millimeters, with 3-millimeter bleed and a minimum 12-millimeter interior safe zone. Use a six-column print grid with generous gutters. Reserve the top 14% for identity and campus, the next 34% for a giant headline, approximately 20% for one food image or useful explanatory statement, and the final 27% for the scan action. Keep the bottom margin clear and stable. Give the QR its own white zone, free of visual debris, rather than treating it as an afterthought.
03 — Type hierarchy and complete copy
Set the headline in Outfit ExtraBold at approximately 74–90 points: “Your campus. / Your next meal.” Use 20–25-point Inter for the description and 17–20-point functional text. Use this exact copy: “MEAL DIRECT”; “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}”; optional “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”; “Your campus. Your next meal.”; “Discover meals and place scheduled orders through your campus link.”; “Scan to explore your campus menu”; and “{{CAMPUS_URL}}”. Let the supplied logo perform the brand-name role when adding a separate “MEAL DIRECT” line would be redundant. Avoid unnecessary introductory paragraphs.
04 — Identity, palette, and logo
Use primary green #0B6B4F, dark green #074C39, mint #BDE8D6, pale green #ECF7F2, white, and optional slate #0F172A/#1E293B/#F8FAFC. Use Outfit display type and Inter functional text. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} intact from Meal Direct’s /logofull.png or /logo.png; preserve proportions, colors, and padding. Never redraw, recolor, crop, or recreate its tagline. Transfer the reference’s editorial restraint, never its purple identity or symbols. Use white paper, a primary-green headline, a slim mint divider, and dark-green CTA text.
05 — Central image and depth
Use one restrained photographic crop of actual campus-relevant food, preferably a naturally lit takeaway meal viewed slightly from above. Keep the visual secondary to the headline and QR. If no appropriate approved image is available, create a strong typography-only version with a small meaningful plate-outline graphic; do not invent a participating vendor. Show only authentic containers and portions. Use low-contrast paper texture in broad background areas if desired, never behind body text or the code. Do not add generic campus buildings, fictional landmarks, or student faces without a reason.
06 — University-name adaptability
Keep university, campus, headline, copy, URL, logo, and QR separately editable. Reserve two lines for {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}; expand the module before shrinking text. Never condense, truncate, or invent abbreviations. Omit a duplicate campus label. Realign neighboring modules after replacement. No university crest or implied institutional endorsement without approval. Position the university module above the headline with a fixed left edge and variable height. For the longest names, retain a minimum approximately 22-point size at A3 and move the headline down; the scan panel must remain intact.
07 — Scan panel and physical usability
Insert the authentic {{QR_ASSET}} on pure white at an initial 45–55-millimeter outer size, including its quiet zone, and enlarge further if the code’s density or viewing conditions demand it. Preserve at least four clear modules on all sides. Place the CTA immediately above the code and the human-readable {{CAMPUS_URL}} below it in dark text. Do not place pin graphics, textures, decorative corners, staples, or instructions inside the white reserve. Validate the code on the final printed sheet at actual size under ordinary indoor noticeboard lighting.
08 — Posting context and exclusions
Design for a visually busy board, using generous negative space and one strong rectangle of information. The first reading should work from a few steps away, while URL and explanation may require a closer view. Keep essential content away from corners where real pins could cover it. Do not mimic an official university notice, administrative seal, academic timetable, or emergency announcement. Avoid ticket stubs, tear-off strips, phone numbers, discount claims, or administrative approvals unless specifically supplied. Use one modest directional cue toward the QR, if useful.
09 — Adaptations and production exports
Create a separate A4 composition at 210 × 297 millimeters with 3-millimeter bleed and 10-millimeter safety; simplify the image area, preserve readable copy, and start its QR at 35–40 millimeters instead of shrinking the entire A3 poster. Build a 1080 × 1350 feed variant with 64-pixel safe margins and a vertically stacked scan card. Reflow the story version to 1080 × 1920. Keep raster images at 300-ppi effective resolution in print. Export PDF/X-4 with fonts embedded and the printer’s confirmed ICC profile, plus RGB digital files.
10 — Final delivery and checks
Deliver named editable layers, linked images, live text, and replaceable QR, plus flat exports. Check facts, rights, spelling, and destination. Inspect A3 and A4 proofs at actual size, then test visibility among unrelated notices. Mark incomplete versions as review proofs; never publish unresolved tokens.

prompts.title: Hostel Poster
prompts.body:
01 — Communication job and factual boundary
Create a warm, useful hostel poster that connects Meal Direct with the ordinary moment of deciding what to eat around study and rest. The desired action is to explore the campus menu and choose among the available scheduled options. Use a supplied hostel name only if the placement and relevant service information are confirmed. Never suggest delivery to every room, guaranteed doorstep service, round-the-clock operation, late-night availability, or unrestricted hostel access. Any fulfillment detail must come from {{VERIFIED_FULFILLMENT_NOTE}} and remain exactly factual.
02 — Format and composition map
Set the primary print artwork to A4 portrait, 210 × 297 millimeters, with 3-millimeter bleed and a 10-millimeter safe area. Divide the page into a 16% identity strip, a 47% photographic scene, and a 37% white information panel. Place the large headline across a deliberately uncluttered portion of the image or a solid green block attached to its edge. Align the bottom panel on two columns: explanation and URL at left, QR at right. Keep the composition calm and domestic rather than nightlife themed.
03 — Type hierarchy and exact copy
Set Outfit Bold or ExtraBold at approximately 39–49 points for “Study break. / Meal plans.” Use Inter at 12–15 points for the description and 14–17 points for the CTA. Include only: “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}”; optional “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}” and “{{HOSTEL_NAME}}”; “Study break. Meal plans.”; “Explore meals and scheduled ordering options through your campus link.”; “Scan to explore”; and “{{CAMPUS_URL}}”. If verified fulfillment information is essential, add its supplied wording as a clearly secondary line. Do not add promises about speed, room service, price, or opening hours.
04 — Identity, palette, and logo
Use primary green #0B6B4F, dark green #074C39, mint #BDE8D6, pale green #ECF7F2, white, and optional slate #0F172A/#1E293B/#F8FAFC. Use Outfit display type and Inter functional text. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} intact from Meal Direct’s /logofull.png or /logo.png; preserve proportions, colors, and padding. Never redraw, recolor, crop, or recreate its tagline. Transfer the reference’s editorial restraint, never its purple identity or symbols. Use pale-green paper, a white utility panel, and an opaque dark-green headline block.
05 — Scene, food, and believable texture
Use an approved documentary-style photograph of a tidy but lived-in student desk: a notebook, a pen, a neutral water bottle, and a realistically portioned meal. Include a student’s hand only if it improves the sense of a real break; anatomy must be accurate and gestures natural. Prefer soft window light or a believable desk lamp, without implying service at the pictured hour. Crop out personal messages and identifiable private information. Avoid luxurious staged dormitories, messy stereotypes, excessive props, repeated hands, plastic-looking food, or visible invented university branding.
06 — Editable location and placement modules
Keep university, campus, headline, copy, URL, logo, and QR separately editable. Reserve two lines for {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}; expand the module before shrinking text. Never condense, truncate, or invent abbreviations. Omit a duplicate campus label. Realign neighboring modules after replacement. No university crest or implied institutional endorsement without approval. If {{HOSTEL_NAME}} is absent, remove its line and keep the spacing intentional. Do not replace it with a fictional accommodation name. Reserve room for a two-line university label above the image; retain the bottom scan panel’s physical dimensions after every location edit.
07 — Scan panel specification
Place the supplied {{QR_ASSET}} on a pure-white reserve at an initial 35–40-millimeter outer width, including at least four modules of clear quiet zone. Keep the code square and unwarped. Print “Scan to explore” outside the quiet zone and place {{CAMPUS_URL}} near the code as a readable fallback. Confirm that the URL and code resolve to the same campus destination. Test the final A4 print at actual size on more than one phone, under the ordinary light of a corridor or common room.
08 — Message restraint and practical detail
Keep the poster’s emotional appeal in the scene, with operational clarity in the bottom panel. A tiny “Scheduled campus meal delivery” descriptor may replace the longer description if space is tight, but do not add both. Avoid bells, moon symbols, “midnight cravings,” delivery scooters outside a hostel, or door-hanging packaging unless those details are specifically verified. Do not use a fabricated phone screen to explain ordering. One simple underline or editorial rule may connect the headline to the food; eliminate floating sticker decorations and multiple CTAs.
09 — Adaptations and export settings
For A3, expand to 297 × 420 millimeters with 3-millimeter bleed and 12-millimeter safety; enlarge type and start the QR at 45–55 millimeters. For 1080 × 1350 digital, keep 64-pixel margins, crop the desk more tightly, and enlarge the campus label and scan action. For a 1080 × 1920 story, stack the photograph above the headline and white utility card; preserve space for a real link sticker. Export print as PDF/X-4 with 300-ppi effective imagery and printer-confirmed ICC settings; export digital as RGB.
10 — Final delivery and checks
Deliver editable text, image, logo, location, and QR layers, plus flat exports. Verify all facts and destination. Review for accidental doorstep or late-night promises. Inspect grayscale printing, actual-size readability, and QR performance. Mark incomplete versions as review proofs; do not publish unresolved tokens.

prompts.title: Counter QR
prompts.body:
01 — Communication job and use context
Create an A6 vendor-counter card that a student can understand while standing at a food counter. Its single job is to open the correct Meal Direct campus route with minimal reading. Treat the QR as the dominant functional object and the campus label as essential confirmation. Mention a vendor only if it is a confirmed participating business and permission to display the card has been obtained. Do not imply that scanning pays for a counter purchase, earns a reward, joins a queue, or places an order automatically.
02 — Exact physical format and zones
Set flat artwork to A6 portrait, 105 × 148 millimeters, with 3-millimeter bleed and a minimum 6-millimeter safe area. Use a centered layout with an intentionally larger gap around the code. Allocate roughly 18% to the logo, 18% to the headline, 10% to the campus label, 35% to the QR, and 19% to the supporting line and fallback URL. Treat these as adjustable proportions: the measured QR and type requirements take priority. Keep the visible card face rectangular and flat, with no simulated folded stand or perspective distortion.
03 — Typography and complete copy
Set “Your next meal / starts here.” in Outfit Bold at approximately 24–30 points, with close but readable line spacing. Set the campus label in Inter Semibold at 10–12 points. Use only the exact proposed copy: “Your next meal starts here.”; “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}”; optional “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”; “Scan to explore your campus menu”; and “{{CAMPUS_URL}}”. Keep the scan instruction at approximately 11–13 points. If a long university name requires more room, remove optional supporting copy before reducing essential text below approximately 9 points. Never add an unsupported offer.
04 — Identity, palette, and logo
Use primary green #0B6B4F, dark green #074C39, mint #BDE8D6, pale green #ECF7F2, white, and optional slate #0F172A/#1E293B/#F8FAFC. Use Outfit display type and Inter functional text. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} intact from Meal Direct’s /logofull.png or /logo.png; preserve proportions, colors, and padding. Never redraw, recolor, crop, or recreate its tagline. Transfer the reference’s editorial restraint, never its purple identity or symbols. Keep two-thirds of the card white, with a green headline and pale-green footer. For compact print, use the icon asset with adjacent plain “Meal Direct” text; do not shrink the padded full logo until unreadable.
05 — Deliberately minimal visual direction
Prefer a typography-and-code composition with no food photography. This card is an instrument for a quick scan, and every extra element competes with that action. If the client explicitly requires a food cue, use one tiny verified food crop at a corner that cannot intrude on the code or URL; do not make it a second focal point. Use flat colors, crisp edges, and no texture. Avoid decorative scanning brackets, phone mockups, glossy reflections, heavy shadows, gradient backgrounds, and a giant arrow pointing into the QR’s white reserve.
06 — Editable campus and optional vendor modules
Keep university, campus, headline, copy, URL, logo, and QR separately editable. Reserve two lines for {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}; expand the module before shrinking text. Never condense, truncate, or invent abbreviations. Omit a duplicate campus label. Realign neighboring modules after replacement. No university crest or implied institutional endorsement without approval. A confirmed vendor attribution, if needed, must read “Available from {{VERIFIED_VENDOR_NAME}}” only when factually accurate. Prefer a text-only attribution instead of a second logo. If a vendor logo is required, use its approved asset in a separate secondary module and remove other optional content to preserve QR scale.
07 — QR dimensions and technical integrity
Use {{QR_ASSET}} as a genuine supplied code, preferably vector or sufficiently high-resolution raster. Start at 40–45 millimeters outer width including the quiet zone; adjust upward if module density requires. Keep a pure-white background and at least four clear modules on every side. Do not round the QR’s data modules, recolor it for decoration, insert a logo, add a frame that touches its quiet zone, or generate a replacement pattern. Keep the source aspect ratio exact and check that export has not blurred the edges.
08 — Placement-aware scan guidance
Put “Scan to explore your campus menu” immediately above or below the white reserve, with enough separation to protect the quiet zone. Show {{CAMPUS_URL}} in plain readable text as the fallback; use only a supplied working short route if the full address is too long. Never invent a shortened URL. Test the code in the intended clear holder or stand because reflections and curvature can affect scanning. Avoid a glossy laminate if it causes scan failures, and keep the card away from surfaces likely to cover its lower edge.
09 — Reflow and production exports
For a square 1080 × 1080 digital card, enlarge the headline and code while retaining generous spacing; do not merely photograph the printed card. For a 1080 × 1350 feed post, maintain 64-pixel margins and expand the campus and explanation modules slightly. For a 1080 × 1920 story, stack the same hierarchy and add a separate real link-sticker area. Export print PDF/X-4 with embedded fonts, sharp QR edges, and a printer-confirmed ICC profile. Any optional raster photograph must resolve at 300 ppi at final size.
10 — Final delivery and checks
Deliver editable text, identity, location, and QR layers, plus flat exports. Check spelling and destination. Print at actual A6 size and test normal counter distance, holder glare, and multiple phones. Inspect code edges after export. Mark unresolved versions as review proofs; a failed scan means the design is unfinished.

prompts.title: Launch Event
prompts.body:
01 — Communication job and release conditions
Create a launch-event announcement that makes the occasion feel welcoming and gives students all the facts needed to attend. The first read is the event announcement, the second is the date and venue, and the third is the RSVP or information action. Use only a confirmed event, with an approved date, time, campus, venue, and event link. If any essential logistics are missing, produce a clearly labeled review proof. Never invent free food, prizes, entertainers, sponsors, limited spaces, registration requirements, or access conditions.
02 — Format and distinctive composition
Design the main digital poster at 1080 × 1350 pixels with 64-pixel safe margins and a 12-column grid. Use an editorial event-sheet concept: an oversized two-line invitation at upper left, a strong date-and-time block at upper right, and a quiet structured logistics panel below. Allocate about 15% to identity and university, 28% to headline, 22% to date and place, 15% to one approved image or simple food object, and 20% to the action rail. Use asymmetry through scale and alignment, not scattered decorations.
03 — Exact copy and typographic roles
Set Outfit ExtraBold at 92–112 pixels for “Meet Meal Direct.” and Inter for all event facts. Include this proposed copy only: “CAMPUS LAUNCH EVENT”; “Meet Meal Direct.”; “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}”; optional “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”; “{{EVENT_TITLE}}”; “{{CONFIRMED_DATE}}”; “{{CONFIRMED_TIME}} {{TIME_ZONE_IF_NEEDED}}”; “{{CONFIRMED_VENUE}}”; “See event details”; and “{{EVENT_URL}}”. If the destination genuinely provides RSVP, replace the CTA with “Scan to RSVP”. Keep logistics at 32–42 pixels and secondary copy at 26–30 pixels. Omit a duplicate event title when it repeats the main headline.
04 — Identity, palette, and logo
Use primary green #0B6B4F, dark green #074C39, mint #BDE8D6, pale green #ECF7F2, white, and optional slate #0F172A/#1E293B/#F8FAFC. Use Outfit display type and Inter functional text. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} intact from Meal Direct’s /logofull.png or /logo.png; preserve proportions, colors, and padding. Never redraw, recolor, crop, or recreate its tagline. Transfer the reference’s editorial restraint, never its purple identity or symbols. Use a green event field, white logistics panel, and one mint date marker.
05 — Image and atmosphere direction
Use an approved photograph connected to the actual event or a restrained still life of an accurately represented meal and takeaway container. If there is no actual event image, do not fabricate a crowd, stage, branded booth, celebrity appearance, or venue installation. Favor natural directional light and believable shadows. Let a single cropped food object overlap the green and white fields slightly, creating depth without covering logistics. Avoid confetti, fireworks, chrome lettering, concert-poster clichés, flashing neon, unverified campus landmarks, and imagery that makes the event appear larger than confirmed.
06 — Editable campus and event modules
Keep university, campus, headline, copy, URL, logo, and QR separately editable. Reserve two lines for {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}; expand the module before shrinking text. Never condense, truncate, or invent abbreviations. Omit a duplicate campus label. Realign neighboring modules after replacement. No university crest or implied institutional endorsement without approval. Give date, time, venue, and action independent fields, with fixed labels and flexible values. Allow a long venue to wrap across two or three readable lines. Do not force different campus events into identical line lengths. Use unambiguous date wording supplied by the organizer; check weekday consistency when a weekday is included.
07 — QR and destination choice
Place the authentic {{QR_ASSET}} on pure white in the action rail, initially around 200–220 pixels outer width for the feed poster, with at least four clear modules on every side. Its destination must match {{EVENT_URL}}, not automatically reuse the campus ordering link. If the event page and campus route differ, keep the event action primary and omit the second route to avoid confusion. Put the CTA outside the quiet zone. Never portray the QR as a ticket, payment confirmation, or guaranteed admission pass unless that function is explicitly verified.
08 — Additional facts and negative constraints
Add {{APPROVED_EVENT_DETAILS}} only when they change an attendance decision, such as a confirmed eligibility rule or registration deadline. Limit this to one short, readable line beneath the venue; do not bury essential restrictions in decorative fine print. Do not add “everyone welcome,” “free entry,” “walk in,” or “bring a friend” unless the organizer confirms those conditions. Never substitute a university logo for a location label. The design must remain celebratory through proportion, color, and typography rather than through unsupported claims or a crowded programme.
09 — Adaptations and production requirements
For a 1080 × 1920 story, stack headline, date/time, venue, image, and QR card, leaving platform-interface space and a real link-sticker zone. For A3 print, use 297 × 420 millimeters, 3-millimeter bleed, 12-millimeter safety, and a 45–55-millimeter outer QR as a starting point. Reflow to A4 separately with a 35–40-millimeter QR. Keep images at 300-ppi effective resolution. Export PDF/X-4 with the printer-confirmed ICC profile and RGB digital files; embed fonts and preserve sharp code modules.
10 — Final delivery and checks
Deliver editable logistics, image, text, logo, and QR layers, plus flat exports. Obtain an organizer’s final check of date, time, venue, RSVP behavior, and access conditions. Confirm the code opens the event destination. Inspect at 25% and 100%. Mark incomplete versions as review proofs.

prompts.title: Food Challenge
prompts.body:
01 — Communication job and responsible concept
Create a friendly campus preference challenge around “Jollof or Swallow?” The objective is conversation and food discovery, not competitive consumption. Treat both choices with equal respect and visual weight. Do not create an eating stunt, a timed challenge, a reward scheme, a gambling mechanic, or a claim that a particular dish has already won. Use the campus menu as the default scan destination. A vote CTA is allowed only when a working verified poll has been supplied; a normal menu link must never be described as a poll.
02 — Primary format and split composition
Build a 1080 × 1350-pixel feed artwork with 64-pixel safe margins and a 12-column grid. Divide the hero zone into two balanced photographic fields separated by a clean vertical boundary. Place the question across the top 25%, the two dishes across the middle 47%, and a compact campus and action strip across the lower 28%. Set a small “OR” on the division line, but keep it away from the food detail. Use scale and a disciplined split for energy rather than lightning bolts, boxing gloves, or battle graphics.
03 — Exact copy and hierarchy
Set “Jollof or / Swallow?” in Outfit ExtraBold at approximately 106–124 pixels, with the two food labels at 42–54 pixels and support text in Inter at 28–32 pixels. Use this default copy: “CAMPUS FOOD TALK”; “Jollof or Swallow?”; “JOLLOF”; “SWALLOW”; “What are you choosing?”; “Explore your campus menu”; “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}”; optional “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”; and “{{CAMPUS_URL}}”. For a digital comment-focused version, “Tell us your pick in the comments” may replace the scan CTA. Do not ask for comments on a printed poster.
04 — Identity, palette, and logo
Use primary green #0B6B4F, dark green #074C39, mint #BDE8D6, pale green #ECF7F2, white, and optional slate #0F172A/#1E293B/#F8FAFC. Use Outfit display type and Inter functional text. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} intact from Meal Direct’s /logofull.png or /logo.png; preserve proportions, colors, and padding. Never redraw, recolor, crop, or recreate its tagline. Transfer the reference’s editorial restraint, never its purple identity or symbols. Use pale green and mint for equally weighted dish fields, with dark-green lettering.
05 — Equal and accurate food photography
Use approved images of a recognizable jollof dish and a recognizable swallow-and-soup serving. Match camera angle, lighting direction, crop scale, and plating prominence so the comparison feels fair. Preserve real food texture and credible portions. Do not depict either dish as dirty, inferior, comic, or excessive. If the photographs are illustrative rather than vendor-specific, avoid vendor names and do not imply both dishes are currently sold on the campus route. Never alter a verified vendor dish with invented proteins, garnishes, or side items just to make it more competitive.
06 — Editable campus and conversation modules
Keep university, campus, headline, copy, URL, logo, and QR separately editable. Reserve two lines for {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}; expand the module before shrinking text. Never condense, truncate, or invent abbreviations. Omit a duplicate campus label. Realign neighboring modules after replacement. No university crest or implied institutional endorsement without approval. Keep both dish labels as separate live text elements, allowing later approved food pairings without rebuilding the entire layout. When a pairing changes, replace both images and all related text consistently. Do not carry over an old poll question, result, or category label into the new version.
07 — QR behavior and alternate poll version
For the default discovery version, insert {{QR_ASSET}} on a pure-white reserve at about 200–220 pixels outer width and label it “Explore your campus menu”. Preserve at least four modules of quiet zone and show {{CAMPUS_URL}} nearby. For an actual poll version, replace both the code and fallback route with {{POLL_QR_ASSET}} and {{VERIFIED_POLL_URL}}, and use “Scan to choose your side”. Never reuse the menu code with voting language. Keep code modules untouched, unwarped, high contrast, and free of decorative food shapes.
08 — Interaction limits and supporting details
Choose one primary interaction per final artwork: comments, a verified poll, or menu exploration. If secondary discovery information is retained, make it visually subordinate and remove the QR when it competes with the main interaction. Do not display percentage bars, vote counts, student quotations, rankings, or “campus winner” labels without verified results and a relevant date. Avoid nutritional superiority claims or mockery of regional food preferences. Keep the tone curious, sociable, and inclusive. The challenge should invite a preference, not pressure anyone to eat more or spend money.
09 — Reflow and output adaptations
For a 1080 × 1920 story, stack the two food panels vertically and reserve a clear platform poll-sticker area if a real poll will be added in-platform; do not bake in a fake interactive sticker. Keep 64-pixel side margins. For A3 print, use 297 × 420 millimeters, 3-millimeter bleed, 12-millimeter safety, and a 45–55-millimeter outer QR; use scan language instead of comments. Export print PDF/X-4 with 300-ppi images and a printer-confirmed ICC profile. Export digital artwork in RGB.
10 — Final delivery and checks
Deliver independently editable food, title, location, identity, and QR layers, plus flat exports. Verify actual destination behavior, image rights, and equal treatment of both foods. Inspect at 25% and 100%. Ensure no invented vendor offering or poll result appears. Mark incomplete versions as review proofs.

prompts.title: Campus Partner
prompts.body:
01 — Communication job and verification gate
Create a credible collaboration announcement for Meal Direct and a real campus or community partner. Its purpose is to explain what the partnership means for students, then direct them to the appropriate verified information or campus route. Use only a collaboration approved by both parties, with supplied logo assets and exact scope. A student association, residence community, or independent group must not be presented as the university itself. Never imply institutional endorsement, exclusivity, an official procurement relationship, or campus-wide coverage unless the agreement explicitly supports it.
02 — Primary format and editorial layout
Build the main artwork at 1080 × 1350 pixels, with 64-pixel safe margins and an invisible 12-column grid. Use a mostly white announcement sheet. Reserve the top 20% for a disciplined two-logo partnership row, the next 25% for a bold approved headline, the middle 25% for a plain-language explanation, and the bottom 30% for campus context and a single action. Use one pale-green vertical accent or horizontal rule to organize the page. Keep substantial negative space so the relationship reads as clear information rather than decorative co-branding.
03 — Complete copy and typography
Set {{APPROVED_PARTNERSHIP_HEADLINE}} in Outfit Bold at approximately 78–98 pixels, with deliberate line breaks and a maximum of three lines. If an approved general headline is needed, propose “Working together / on campus.” for review. Use this copy framework: “CAMPUS COLLABORATION”; “Meal Direct × {{PARTNER_NAME}}”; “{{APPROVED_COLLABORATION_SCOPE}}”; “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}”; optional “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”; and “Explore your campus link”. Set the scope in Inter at 32–38 pixels, limited to one concise factual paragraph. Do not substitute a vague benefits promise for a missing approved scope.
04 — Meal Direct identity and partner logo handling
Use primary green #0B6B4F, dark green #074C39, mint #BDE8D6, pale green #ECF7F2, white, and optional slate #0F172A/#1E293B/#F8FAFC. Use Outfit display type and Inter functional text. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} intact from Meal Direct’s /logofull.png or /logo.png; preserve proportions, colors, and padding. Never redraw, recolor, crop, or recreate its tagline. Transfer the reference’s editorial restraint, never its purple identity or symbols. Place the approved partner logo beside Meal Direct with equal optical respect, intact proportions, and required clear space.
05 — Visual concept and optional imagery
Default to typography, identity, and one subtle real-world cue, such as an approved photograph of an actual shared activity. If no verified image exists, omit photography; do not generate a handshake, signing ceremony, university gate, event banner, or group photograph that appears to document an event that never occurred. A restrained paper texture may occupy the background, but keep logo areas clean and flat. Avoid seals, certificate motifs, official-looking crests, ribbon badges, and prestige symbols. Credibility must come from accurate names and a clear scope of work.
06 — Flexible campus and partner modules
Keep university, campus, headline, copy, URL, logo, and QR separately editable. Reserve two lines for {{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}; expand the module before shrinking text. Never condense, truncate, or invent abbreviations. Omit a duplicate campus label. Realign neighboring modules after replacement. No university crest or implied institutional endorsement without approval. Allow {{PARTNER_NAME}} up to two lines in its text attribution, separate from the logo row. If the partner’s long name makes the composition crowded, enlarge the information area and reduce optional visual content. Do not abbreviate a partner or university without an approved short form.
07 — QR, fallback route, and action integrity
Use the supplied genuine QR on pure white, beginning at approximately 200–220 pixels outer width for the feed version and preserving at least four modules of quiet zone. If the action is campus discovery, use {{QR_ASSET}} with {{CAMPUS_URL}} and the CTA “Explore your campus link”. If the partnership requires a dedicated explanation, use a verified code for {{PARTNERSHIP_DETAILS_URL}} and change the CTA to “Read about the collaboration”. Keep only one principal destination.
