Do not suggest that the code verifies institutional approval or enrolls students automatically.
08 — Scope clarity and prohibited inference
State practical scope in approved language, such as a confirmed awareness activity or community referral arrangement, only when supplied. Do not add benefits, discounts, delivery access, employment opportunities, or official status that the agreement does not provide. Keep logos away from language that could attribute every claim to both organizations. If either party requires a disclaimer or attribution line, preserve its approved wording and a readable minimum size. Do not invent that line yourself. The finished announcement must clearly identify which organization is collaborating and what has actually been agreed.
09 — Reflow and production specifications
For a 1080 × 1920 story, stack the logo row, headline, scope paragraph, and action card, maintaining 64-pixel side margins and clear interface space. For an A4 announcement, use 210 × 297 millimeters, 3-millimeter bleed, 10-millimeter safety, and a 35–40-millimeter outer QR. A3 may expand to a 45–55-millimeter code with 12-millimeter safety. Preserve the partner’s optical logo balance across formats. Export print PDF/X-4 with printer-confirmed ICC settings and 300-ppi photography, plus RGB digital files.
10 — Final delivery and checks
Deliver editable logos, scope, location, headline, and QR layers, plus flat exports. Verify names, rights, factual scope, and destination. Follow the supplied partner approval process. Review whether the overall design implies a broader agreement. Inspect at 25% and 100%. Mark incomplete versions as review proofs.

prompts.title: Pocket Flyer
prompts.body:
01 — Communication job and handout context
Create a pocket-sized campus activation flyer that a student can understand immediately, retain, and scan later. The message is that Meal Direct provides a campus route for discovering meals and placing scheduled orders. The single desired action is to explore that route. Confirm the campus link is active before using ordering language. Keep the design useful at its actual physical size: this is a small printed object, so detailed information belongs on the destination page. Never compensate for missing facts with invented discounts, referral rewards, delivery promises, or app-store badges.
02 — Main format and two-sided architecture
Use A6 portrait, 105 × 148 millimeters, as the preferred duplex master with 3-millimeter bleed and 6-millimeter safety. On the front, allocate approximately 20% to identity and location, 40% to the headline, and 40% to a single food crop or solid green field. On the back, place a concise explanation above a dominant white QR reserve and the fallback URL below. Keep front and back aligned to the same grid and visual identity. Provide clearly labeled FRONT and BACK production files outside the artwork area, never printed as visible headings.
03 — Front copy and type hierarchy
Set the front headline in Outfit ExtraBold at approximately 29–36 points: “Campus meals. / One place / to explore.” Use Inter Semibold at 10–12 points for the university and campus label. Include only the supplied logo, “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}”, optional “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”, and the headline on the front. Avoid a second competing tagline. Preserve a clear reading order even when the card is held at arm’s length. If the university name needs two lines, expand the top module and slightly reduce the image area rather than shrinking the campus label excessively.
04 — Reverse copy and information limits
Use the reverse copy: “Meet Meal Direct.”; “Discover meals and scheduled ordering options through your campus link.”; “Scan to explore”; and “{{CAMPUS_URL}}”. Set the introductory line at approximately 18–22 points, body text at 10–12 points, and CTA at 12–14 points. Keep all necessary text at approximately 9 points or larger after proofing. Do not add an unverified ordering process, support number, payment method, service schedule, minimum order, or small-print disclaimer. If factual qualifications are necessary, shorten the main body or use the larger A6 format.
05 — Identity, palette, and logo
Use primary green #0B6B4F, dark green #074C39, mint #BDE8D6, pale green #ECF7F2, white, and optional slate #0F172A/#1E293B/#F8FAFC. Use Outfit display type and Inter functional text. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} intact from Meal Direct’s /logofull.png or /logo.png; preserve proportions, colors, and padding. Never redraw, recolor, crop, or recreate its tagline. Transfer the reference’s editorial restraint, never its purple identity or symbols. Use a green front and white reverse. Avoid unapproved logo inversion. For compact print, use the icon asset with adjacent plain “Meal Direct” text; do not shrink the padded full logo until unreadable.
06 — Photograph and editable modules
If using a front photograph, choose one approved, realistic meal crop with natural side light, recognizable ingredients, and authentic packaging. Do not imply vendor availability through generic imagery. Keep the image separate from all typography and omit it if the smaller format becomes crowded. Build live editable university, campus, headline, description, URL, logo, and QR layers. Reserve two university-name lines and adjust the vertical layout for longer replacements. Do not add university crests or invented campus landmarks. The same flyer system must remain convincing with photography removed.
07 — QR specification and physical scan test
Place the genuine {{QR_ASSET}} on a flat pure-white reserve at an initial 28–32-millimeter outer width, including a quiet zone of at least four modules on every side. This is a starting size, not a guarantee: enlarge it for dense codes or poor print conditions. Keep all nearby text outside the quiet zone and use dark code modules without decoration. Show {{CAMPUS_URL}} as a readable fallback. Test a final physical print at 100% scale on multiple phones; verify both sides are correctly oriented and the code opens the named campus.
08 — A7 simplification rather than reduction
If A7 is requested, create a separate one-sided 74 × 105-millimeter design with 3-millimeter bleed and approximately 5-millimeter safety. Keep only the approved logo, university label, “Explore your campus menu”, the 28–32-millimeter outer QR, and the fallback route. Remove the photograph and explanatory paragraph. Do not scale the A6 duplex layout down. If the university name and URL cannot remain comfortably legible, retain A6 or request an approved shorter displayed route rather than fabricating one. Protect scan usability before adding decorative elements.
09 — Digital adaptations and production
Recompose a 1080 × 1350 feed version with 64-pixel margins, showing the front message and scan action on a single flat canvas. For a 1080 × 1920 story, place the headline above the photograph or green field and the campus route in a lower utility card; provide a real link-sticker area. Do not use a mockup of both flyer sides as the primary digital campaign asset. Export print PDF/X-4 with embedded fonts, 300-ppi effective photographs, and printer-confirmed ICC settings; provide RGB digital exports.
10 — Final delivery and checks
Deliver editable front and back masters with live text, linked images, and replaceable QR, plus flat exports. Verify spelling, destination, and facts. Check duplex alignment, bleed, long-name variants, handheld readability, and scanning after finishing. Keep mockups separate from production files. Mark incomplete versions as review proofs.

prompts.title: Packaging Insert
prompts.body:
01 — Communication job and context
Create a compact packaging insert that acknowledges the current meal and makes a future visit to the campus menu easy. Its purpose is repeat discovery, not an unsupported promotion. The insert must feel useful and considerate when someone opens a delivered order. Use a tone of simple appreciation without pretending to know the customer’s name, purchase history, dietary needs, satisfaction, or future preference. Never invent cashback, loyalty points, a referral reward, a second-order discount, free delivery, or a guaranteed delivery schedule.
02 — Exact format and duplex layout
Use A7 portrait, 74 × 105 millimeters, double-sided, with 3-millimeter bleed and approximately 5-millimeter safe margins. Make the front a calm brand moment: a small intact logo at top, a confident headline in the center, and the university label below. Make the reverse a practical white scan card with a short introduction, QR, and fallback URL. Align both sides to a simple centered grid. Prioritize physically readable text and a full-size code; omit decorative content before compromising either. Keep the final production pages flat and correctly oriented.
03 — Front copy and typography
Set “Enjoy this meal. / Discover your next.” in Outfit Bold at approximately 22–27 points, allowing three lines if necessary. Use Inter at 9–11 points for “{{UNIVERSITY_NAME}}” and optional “{{CAMPUS_NAME}}”. Add no extra slogan, signature, or personalized name. The complete front copy is the headline and the supplied location labels alongside the genuine logo. Use comfortable line spacing, optical centering, and generous gaps between logo, headline, and location. Do not add a printed “thank you” from a specific vendor unless that attribution is actually approved.
04 — Reverse copy and useful hierarchy
Use this exact reverse copy: “Keep your campus link handy.”; “Explore meals and scheduled ordering options.”; “Scan for your next pick”; and “{{CAMPUS_URL}}”. Set the first line at approximately 12–15 points in Outfit Semibold and the body at 9–10 points in Inter. Keep the CTA around 10–12 points. If the available area becomes crowded, remove the explanatory body line first. Do not add a second QR, survey, social icon row, or contact block by default. The repeat-discovery route must remain the single visual and functional focus.
05 — Identity, palette, and logo
Use primary green #0B6B4F, dark green #074C39, mint #BDE8D6, pale green #ECF7F2, white, and optional slate #0F172A/#1E293B/#F8FAFC. Use Outfit display type and Inter functional text. Place {{LOGO_PRIMARY}} intact from Meal Direct’s /logofull.png or /logo.png; preserve proportions, colors, and padding. Never redraw, recolor, crop, or recreate its tagline. Transfer the reference’s editorial restraint, never its purple identity or symbols. Use a pale-green front and white reverse; prevent dark-ink show-through behind the QR. For compact print, use the icon asset with adjacent plain “Meal Direct” text; do not shrink the padded full logo until unreadable.
06 — Material, imagery, and modularity
Prefer a typography-only insert with a warm, restrained paper feel. A small natural photographic detail is optional only on a larger-format adaptation; do not crowd the A7 master with food images. Keep texture away from the reverse and all text. Use separate editable layers for campus, university, headline, logo, URL, and QR. Allow the university label to wrap to two lines without reducing it below a comfortable proofed size. Use no university crest, official seal, invented vendor mark, or unverified sustainability certification. Confirm stock and any food-contact placement requirements with the packaging supplier.
07 — QR reserve and scan integrity
Place the authentic {{QR_ASSET}} at an initial 28–32-millimeter outer width, including at least four modules of white quiet zone. Keep the QR wholly on one side, square, crisp, and free of folds, perforations, adhesive areas, textures, or graphic overlays. Preserve genuine code modules and never generate a decorative substitute. Place the CTA above the reserve and {{CAMPUS_URL}} below it without invading the quiet zone. Increase the code size or simplify surrounding text if density makes scanning unreliable; the stated range must not override actual test results.
08 — Repeat-discovery boundaries and optional support
The insert may encourage a return visit but must not assume the next order will use identical vendors, prices, menus, or delivery options. Avoid “reorder in one tap” unless that exact function is verified. Do not describe the QR as tracking the current order or contacting support when it opens a campus menu. If {{VERIFIED_SUPPORT_ROUTE}} is essential, place a small separate text-only line labeled “Order help:” and remove optional body copy to make room. Do not invent a support number or use an unverified address.
09 — Adaptation and production directions
For an A6 insert, use 105 × 148 millimeters, 3-millimeter bleed, and 6-millimeter safety, enlarging the text and QR rather than adding unnecessary information. For 1080 × 1350 digital, recompose the appreciation headline and discovery action on one canvas with 64-pixel margins. A 1080 × 1920 story should stack the message, campus label, and action card with space for an actual link sticker. Export print PDF/X-4 with embedded fonts and the printer-confirmed ICC profile; any raster artwork must be 300 ppi at final size. Export digital in RGB.
10 — Final delivery and checks
Deliver editable front and back masters with separate location, identity, copy, and QR layers, plus flat exports. Verify facts and destination. Test actual printed inserts on multiple phones; check show-through, glare, trimming, duplex orientation, long labels, and handheld readability. Mark incomplete versions as review proofs.
